title: Applied AI Engineer, Codex
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. For software engineering organizations, this means helping customers adopt Codex and other OpenAI capabilities across the software development lifecycle—transforming how teams plan, build, test, review, and deliver software.

We work directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities, design and implement AI-powered development workflows, and scale what works across engineering organizations. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products, reusable architectures, and technical patterns that help developers everywhere get more value from Codex.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex, you will partner directly with leading engineering organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that transform how software is developed. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from workflow and use-case selection through prototyping, evaluation, production rollout, and scaled adoption.

You will work alongside engineering teams to build advanced AI coding workflows, integrations, automations, and evaluation systems—often using Codex itself as part of your development process. You will help customers make technical decisions involving model behavior, agentic workflows, developer environments, security, reliability, evaluation, and operational readiness, while ensuring deployments translate into measurable improvements in engineering productivity and software delivery.

You will work closely with OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, Sales, and the broader Codex organization, translating real-world deployment experience into high-signal product and model feedback. Success is measured by production systems, sustained developer adoption, and meaningful improvements to how engineering organizations build software—not simply successful demonstrations or enablement activity.

This role is based in our London office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Partner directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities for Codex and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

  • Design, build, and deploy AI-powered software development workflows that improve how engineering teams plan, write, test, review, debug, and deliver software.

  • Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, workflow automations, and production accelerators—often using Codex as part of your own development process.

  • Help customers progress from promising experiments to reliable production workflows, sustained developer adoption, and scaled impact across engineering organizations.

  • Design systematic approaches for evaluating AI coding systems using representative software engineering tasks, automated graders, production signals, and developer feedback.

  • Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, tools, developer environments, integrations, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and operational readiness.

  • Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive technical blockers toward resolution.

  • Lead technical deep dives, workshops, and hands-on enablement that help engineering teams understand and adopt advanced AI coding workflows effectively and safely.

  • Gather high-fidelity insights from real-world Codex deployments and translate them into clear product proposals, model feedback, and technical requirements for OpenAI Product, Research, and Engineering teams.

  • Create reusable architectures, tooling, examples, guides, and technical patterns—including contributions to resources such as the OpenAI Cookbook—that accelerate future Codex deployments.

  • Influence customer engineering strategy by helping technical leaders understand how AI coding systems can reshape their software development lifecycle, engineering practices, and organizational workflows.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering software or AI systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, developer tooling, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

  • Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, integrations, or production engineering—not only program, enablement, or stakeholder management.

  • Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across modern software development environments; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

  • Are an active user of AI coding tools and have developed a strong point of view on how AI can improve developer productivity and software engineering workflows.

  • Enjoy building high-signal prototypes, integrations, automations, and production solutions that demonstrate and deliver what AI coding systems can enable.

  • Understand how to evaluate AI coding systems systematically, including designing representative tasks, automated evaluations, production signals, and mechanisms for incorporating developer feedback.

  • Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as developer tooling integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

  • Can connect technical decisions to developer workflows, adoption, engineering productivity, and measurable business outcomes.

  • Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, engineering leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

  • Are comfortable leading technical workshops and hands-on sessions that help engineering organizations adopt new development workflows and technologies.

  • Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous and rapidly evolving environments.

  • Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; deep prior experience with OpenAI products is not required.

  • Are able to speak English and French fluently.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

title: Artworker / Jr Designer
descriptionHtml:
About Caddy Comps

Caddy Comps is the UK's leading golf prize competition platform. Founded in 2021 and based in Stamford, Lincolnshire, we've awarded over £15m in prizes to more than 50,000 winners and hold a 5-star Trustpilot rating from 8,400+ reviews.

We're now building the marketing team and infrastructure to take us to the next level, and this role is a key part of that.

The Role

This is a hands-on production design role.

Our Creative Designer sets the look and feel of the brand. Your job is to roll it out, accurately and at pace, across every place a customer sees us: paid ads, emails, social, the website and the app.

We launch new competitions every week, and each one needs artwork. Prize imagery, competition tiles, ad creative, email banners, social assets. You'll be the person who makes sure every one of them goes out on time, on brand and pixel-perfect.

This is a role for someone early in their design career who loves the craft of artworking, wants real responsibility, and wants to grow into a designer who originates as well as executes.

Tasks

Artwork & Production

  • Produce artwork for new competitions each week, prize imagery, competition tiles, banners and listings

  • Adapt and resize master designs across formats and channels to exact specifications

  • Retouch, cut out and composite prize and product imagery to a high standard

  • Prepare and export files correctly for web, app, social, email and occasional print

  • Check every asset for accuracy, prices, dates, T&Cs, spelling and brand consistency, before it goes out

Campaign & Channel Design

  • Create static and simple animated ad creative for Meta, TikTok and Google

  • Design email, SMS and push assets for our CRM campaigns

  • Produce social graphics, thumbnails and story assets for the Social Media Manager

  • Design under direction for campaign moments, launches and ambassador activations

title: Associate Product Manager (US Cards)
descriptionHtml:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

In six years, Lendable has built a profitable, market-leading credit card in the UK. In 2023, we brought that playbook to the US and set an even higher bar. This year the US credit card business scaled rapidly: our run rate grew more than 20x in the last six months.

A lot of the work of getting customers through the door is in place. The next stage is about what happens once they’re in: helping them pay on time, giving more credit to the ones who earn it, getting people back on track when they fall behind, and ensuring an intuitive user experience across channels.

If you're excited by fintech, lending and scaling products in a fast-moving environment, this role offers real ownership, impact and room to grow.

About the role

We're hiring a Associate Product Manager to join the product team, and will cover post booking areas including payments, collections, credit limit increases, spend, and the mobile app.

No two weeks look the same. One week you might be sizing an opportunity, the next week sitting with the ops team to understand why customers are calling, or putting a rough version of an idea in front of real customers before anyone builds the proper one. We care more about how quickly we learn than how polished the first attempt looks.

What you'll work on

  • Running experiments across the customer lifecycle, such as how and when we remind people to pay, what gets them to set up autopay, and how we gamify engagement

  • Working with credit risk and data science on how to apply models to new use cases and opportunities

  • Finding cheap, fast ways to test an idea (a manual process, an email, a script) with AI before committing engineering time to it

  • Gathering customer research to get truthful and unbiased reads

  • Building tools and automations with AI that save time for you, the ops team and the wider business

  • Doing whatever it takes to get something live, including the unglamorous parts like unblocking developers, socializing with legal and compliance, or writing the guide for the ops team

What we're looking for

Don’t worry if you don’t meet all these criteria. We'd love to talk to any great candidate that is excited, inquisitive, and a go-getter.

  • 1-4 years in product, strategy, analytics, consulting or operations, with some time spent working closely to product or execution teams to deliver value

  • You ask a lot of questions and you're not satisfied until you understand why something is happening

  • You enjoy forming a hypothesis and finding the quickest way to test it, even if the first version is rough

  • You're comfortable with data: you can write SQL or Python and answer your own questions

  • You're already using AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex in your work or side projects, and you want to see how far they go

  • You're happy to pick up the small jobs, understanding that as a lean product team no job is too unworthy of our attention

  • You like days that look different from each other

  • Bonus: experience in lending, payments, fintech or a fast-growing startup

Keep in mind: you will not be a fit for this role if you're looking for a well-defined backlog to manage, or you'd rather wait until a problem is fully specified before starting on it. Much of what we work on starts as a loose question with multiple options possible.

AI at Lendable

We want to build the most AI-forward financial services company in the world. PMs here make their own dashboards to answer questions that used to need an analyst, build their own agents and workflows to take care of repetitive work, and ship straightforward changes to production themselves. You don't need to be an expert on day one, but we'll expect you to keep pushing what one person can do.

Your team

You'll report to the Senior Product Manager for Customer Management, and work most closely with:

  • A developer and design team split across London and Europe, covering frontend and backend

  • A data science team building models specific to the US business

  • A credit risk team

  • A growth team

  • An operations team

The team spans our London office, remote engineers in Europe, and our office in Arlington, Virginia, near DC, which you'll visit.

Life at Lendable

  • No one here is limited to their lane. If you want to pick up credit analysis, prototype a feature or fix something in ops, you will be supported.

  • Work from home Mondays and Fridays, and be in the office Tuesday to Thursday, with lunches prepared by our top-tier in-house chefs

  • Top-tier private health insurance

  • Offsites for the US Cards product and engineering team, and an annual whole-company trip abroad (previously Turkey and France)

Interview process

We respect your time and move quickly:

  1. Intro call (remote) - 30 minutes with the hiring manager

  2. Take-home exercise (remote) - a practical product challenge in your own time, followed by a video debrief with two members of the product team

  3. Final round (in our London office) - typically with the CPO and US Cards MD, Engineering Manager, Head of Product and hiring manager

Life at Lendable

  • Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

  • Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

  • Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members

  • Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations

  • Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations

Please note: The availability and details of specific benefits vary by location and role. For more information, please speak to your Talent Partner.

descriptionHtml:

dnl is a fast-growing AI startup building AI-first solutions for auditing. Our software automates disclosure checklists and other document-heavy audit work for audit firms and corporate clients, so professionals can spend their time on judgment instead of manual checking. Our mission: transform auditing through AI and help auditors work smarter than ever before.

The role

You bring many years of audit experience and use it to expand our platform conceptually. You co-decide which audit problems we solve next, design how our platform addresses them, and grow the value dnl contributes to every engagement. This role is for auditors, not career product managers: audit experience is required, product management experience is not.

You know first-hand where audits lose time, where risks are missed and which workarounds teams rely on. You don't need to code. You need to think in structured processes and want to build the tools you always wished you had. You work closely with our engineering and AI team, our customers and the management team.

  • Structured, analytical thinking: you can sketch a decision tree and define the right outcome for edge cases

  • The ability to explain complex topics simply to engineers, customers and decision-makers

  • Hands-on experience with AI tools

  • Motivation to reshape the profession, not just to take the next career step

  • Native or near-native English - German is a plus

  • You are Europe-based

Nice to have

  • Experience in product management, audit methodology or audit tooling/digitisation projects

  • WP/CPA/ACA qualification or working towards one

Benefits

title: Backend Engineer | 36labs
descriptionHtml:
Role: Backend Engineer

Company: 36 Labs

Location: London, Baker Street office, four days a week (a move to Primrose Hill is likely within a couple of months). London-based candidates only. No relocation and no visa sponsorship in this hiring cycle.

Job Type: Full-time

About 36 Labs

36 Labs is an applied AI research firm in London. It works on a problem most models are still bad at: making creative decisions, and explaining why they were made. The team wants models to reason creatively, more like a person would.

Today the product is a harness that sits over any frontier model, video generation models in particular. It handles ideation, generation and distribution end to end, and the content goes out to real audiences. The results feed a data loop that keeps improving the harness. The first use case is music marketing, and the clients are the major labels, including Sony, Warner and Universal.

The company has been profitable since it started operating. It is closing its first seed round within the next couple of weeks, and the round was oversubscribed. The team is about ten people, with four engineers who report to the CTO. He is still very hands-on in the code.

You would join at a big moment. V3 of the harness is being released, which is a huge scope of work. A migration to Cloudflare is planned, and it falls mostly to the backend engineer. The stack is Python, TypeScript, Postgres, LLM and generative model APIs, and open-weight models.

What you are expected to do:

  • Migrate many of the company's systems to Cloudflare. This is your first big task.

  • Work on a bit of everything as needed. Engineers here are not siloed, and the structure is flat.

  • Take a direction from the team and own it, without close supervision.

  • Explain your approach back to the team and talk it through. Disagreement is welcome.

What you need to succeed:

Experience

  • You have 4+ years of experience, including years building and running back-end systems in production. You know how they were deployed and operated.

  • You are hands-on as an engineer in the AI-native era, and you keep reviewing how you work. You follow the latest stacks, models and practices.

  • You have owned something real before. Ownership and leadership are visible in your CV and your projects.

How you work

  • You take initiative and work independently. The culture here is high agency: it is often easier to ask for forgiveness than permission.

  • You communicate clearly and can explain your ideas to the team and discuss them. No big ego.

  • You are comfortable with an extremely fast pace and very little stability.

Practicalities

  • You are based in London and happy to be in the office four days a week.

  • You do not need visa sponsorship in this cycle. A visa that expires next June is fine.

  • Nice to have: a degree in computer science, engineering, maths or stats. An MSc or PhD is a real plus. With a BSc only, your track record needs to be really strong.

  • Nice to have: projects beyond your university or company roles. Where you studied matters little, and what you have built matters more.

What you get:

  • Seed-stage experience that builds a wide range of skills and looks good on a CV.

  • Room to move into a more senior role as the CTO gradually steps back from the code to focus on strategy.

  • A company that is profitable, with an oversubscribed first round and another fundraise planned in the next nine to twelve months.

  • Work with the major music labels as clients, and a rare problem: improving creativity in models. The team believes that if creativity in LLMs is solved, human attention is within reach.

  • A big scope from day one: the V3 harness release and the Cloudflare migration.

  • A flat team where direction is given, ownership is yours and challenge is welcome.

How to apply

Send your LinkedIn profile or CV, plus any projects you are proud of, to the recruiter who shared this role. Use the subject line "Backend Engineer – 36 Labs". We screen candidates first, then introduce a small number to the client. The process: a first conversation with Benedict, Head of Operations (CV, projects, motivation, fit), then a technical interview of about 30 minutes with the CTO, then a take-home assessment. An onsite working session happens only if needed. Timelines are quick, but a notice period of around a month is fine.

title: Backend Engineer - Payments Team
descriptionHtml:
Join a fast-growing, listed company with a purpose! Fastned owns and operates a network of 400+ fast charging stations across 10 European countries, allowing electric vehicle drivers to charge their car with 100% green energy in just 15 minutes. Our goal is a European network of 1000 fast charging stations in prime locations, where all electric vehicles can charge with renewable energy from the sun and wind. We have recently been voted best charging network in the UK, France and the Netherlands. If you want to make a difference and work in an informal, international scale-up environment with future prospects, then read on!

Your role

Fastned aims to accelerate the transition towards sustainable mobility by giving fast charging to electric drivers. Part of that mission is making car charging as simple as charging your phone, and paying for it should be just as effortless. As a Backend Engineer in the Payments team, you will help make paying for a charge frictionless, secure and reliable. Drivers can pay through the Fastned app, by QR code or with a contactless card at the charger.

The team owns Fastned’s payments domain end to end. That covers integrations with payment service providers and payment terminals. It also covers the services behind payment methods, wallets, pre-authorisation and session payments, billing, invoicing and dunning. The stakes are high: Fastned handles 23,000+ charging sessions a day, and every one of those payments goes through our systems. We’re now moving towards real-time payments, where each session is paid instantly instead of invoiced later. As we are growing and adding roaming features as a Mobility Service Provider, there are many scale relevant challenges to solve.

We have no legacy systems. You’ll work with Kotlin 2.x, Java 21+, and Spring Boot 4 on most services, AWS, Kubernetes, Kafka, SQL (Postgres), Terraform, GitLab CI/CD and REST APIs to build scalable, fault-tolerant services that drivers and our Finance team rely on every day. We encourage responsible AI usage and provide tooling like Claude Code, Codex, Dust.

You’ll work closely with the other product teams, alongside fellow Backend Engineers, Data, Design, an Engineering Manager and a Product Manager in a Scrum setup. This role suits an engineer who enjoys a complex domain, cares about getting the details right, and wants to grow by taking real ownership of business-critical systems.

Your overall responsibilities include

  • Designing, developing, testing and reviewing reusable, maintainable and scalable code

  • Working AI-first: using AI-augmented engineering, agentic workflows and AI tooling as a natural part of how you design, build, test and review, with judgement for where AI is a multiplier and where humans stay in the loop;

  • Taking operational responsibility for what you build, including monitoring, alerting and incident analysis;

In order to be successful in this role, you bring a strong sense of ownership and a pragmatic, proactive mindset. You enjoy working in a collaborative scale-up environment where things can change quickly and where taking initiative matters.

Additionally, you tick the following boxes:

  • You have 3+ years of professional backend experience, with strong hands-on Kotlin and/or Java experience.

  • You have previous experience in the payments domain.

  • You have experience working in agile teams within an international, multicultural environment.

  • You have experience building and operating microservices in production, using REST APIs, cloud platforms and relational databases.

  • You care about reliability, maintainability and the operational impact of the software you build.

  • You spot opportunities and problems and pick them up yourself instead of waiting for a ticket.

Electric mobility is new territory for you? Don’t worry!

Aufgaben

  • Analyse von Märkten, Customer Journeys & Performance: Du analysierst Märkte, Kampagnen und Kundendaten (z.B. Customer Journeys), identifizierst Potenziale und leitest daraus klare Handlungsempfehlungen für Marketing, Sales und Produkt ab.
  • Mitgestaltung von Data- & AI-Use-Cases: Du wirkst bei der Entwicklung von Use Cases mit – z. B. Personalisierung, Next Best Action/Offer, Churn Prevention oder Kampagnenoptimierung – und hilfst, sie fachlich zu strukturieren.

title: Business Operations & Data Specialist (Finance)
descriptionHtml:
About the role

Every number that reaches our leadership team, our board, and our auditors has to be right the first time — and that is where you come in. As a Business Operations & Data Specialist focused on Finance at Destinus, you are the bridge between the owners of our financial data, the CFO, and the wider finance team and the data in our lakehouse. You own how finance data is defined, where it comes from, how it is produced, and how it reaches the people who make decisions with it.

This is as much an operations role as a reporting one. You will translate what finance needs to know into what the data platform has to deliver, working with our Data Engineers on the finance data in the lakehouse and building the dashboards the CFO and the finance team rely on. You will also improve the processes and systems that create the numbers in the first place, automate the manual work that eats the month, and make our finance data understandable to everyone who needs it, including our AI assistants.

At Destinus, we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing — bringing speed, precision, and innovation to every process that powers our advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). We are a fast-growing international group operating across several European entities, and the standards we hold our financial data to are rising just as quickly. Join us in building a finance reporting foundation that is accurate, traceable, and ready for any question asked of it.

What You'll Do

  • Be the go-to contact between the business owners of finance data — the CFO, accounts payable and receivable, and treasury — and our lakehouse: turn their questions into clear data requirements, and the data back into answers they can act on.
  • Build and maintain Power BI dashboards covering cash flow, receipts and collections, payables, and spend across the group, built on certified lakehouse data.
  • Partner with our Data Engineers on the curated (gold) layer for finance: specify the tables, fields, and business rules — entities, currencies, financial dimensions, intercompany — and validate the result against the ledger before anyone relies on it.
  • Prepare and quality-check entity-level data extractions from our lakehouse and ERP in support of the external audit, and keep audit requests tracked from request to delivery.
  • Define and document finance KPI definitions in our KPI catalog — formulas, inclusions, exclusions, owners, and sources — to a standard that withstands external review.
  • Describe our finance data in plain business language — what each field means, who owns it, and how sensitive it is — for our shared meanings layer, so that colleagues and our AI assistants can use it correctly without having to ask you first.
  • Automate what is manual today: turn recurring spreadsheet work, audit packs, and month-end routines into repeatable processes that largely run themselves.
  • Improve the finance processes and system configuration that create the data, working with the finance team and our ERP specialists, so that issues are fixed at source rather than corrected every month.
  • Help the finance team get more from the tools through training and self-service, so they can answer their own questions.

Requirements

What You’ll Need

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Controlling, Economics, or a related field.
  • A genuine finance background is essential — experience in external or internal audit, controlling, financial reporting, or FP&A. This is not a data role with finance on the side; you need to understand the accounting behind the figures.
  • Confident with general ledger and subledger structures, trial balances, accounts payable and accounts receivable, bank reconciliations, intercompany transactions, and the principles of IFRS.
  • Strong expertise in Power BI (data modeling, DAX, dashboard design, troubleshooting), complemented by advanced Excel skills.
  • Comfortable querying data with SQL and working in a lakehouse or data warehouse environment; experience with Microsoft Fabric or a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture is a plus. You will not build the pipelines — you need to know what to ask for and how to check what comes back.
  • Able to explain data to finance colleagues and accounting logic to technical ones — and to get both sides to agree on one definition.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance is a strong advantage — the general ledger, accounts payable and accounts receivable modules, and the data structures underneath them. We run on D365, and someone who already knows it will be effective months earlier. An interest in improving how the system is configured and used matters as much as knowing where to click.
  • A track record of simplifying or automating a process, not only reporting on it.
  • Experience supporting an external audit, or working in a multi-entity, multi-currency international group, is a strong advantage.
  • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.
  • Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is preferred.

Who You Are

You are precise, and you are curious about where a number came from before you are comfortable reporting it — whether that means reading the ledger or querying the lakehouse. You know the difference between a figure that looks right and a figure that can be traced back to its source, and you care about the second one.

You are not content to rebuild the same report every month. When something is manual, repetitive, or fragile, your instinct is to go upstream and fix it rather than absorb it. You enjoy working with finance colleagues who ask hard questions, and you would rather be challenged on a detail than have it slip through.

Above all, you want your work to be relied on, by the CFO, by the board, and by anyone who audits it.

title: CDI - Head of Finance (Paris)
descriptionHtml:
We are hiring a Head of Finance and to own the finance function end to end, reporting to the CFO: monthly close and reporting, budget and rolling business plan, board materials, cash, audits and the regulatory obligations of a syndic, across our French and German entities.

It is a hands-on role for someone who can do every job in the team and wants to shape the function as the company scales.

With our CFO focused on fundraising and strategic topics, you will be the day-to-day finance decision-maker, working directly with the CEO, the VPs and the German country manager. As Matera grows, including through acquisitions in France and Germany, there is scope to rapidly grow into a VP Finance role.

What you will do

1. Operational finance and business plan (70%) :

  • Own the monthly close of all entities (in France and Germany) and deliver the management reporting pack: P&L, cash, KPIs, reconciliation with the statutory accounts, reporting to investors and banks.

  • Own the annual budget, built with every team lead, and the business plan, updated every month after the close, for France and Germany.

  • Own cash: the cash forecast, collection from customers, bank loans and their covenants, financing files and data rooms.

  • Deliver the statutory audits in France and Germany and the annual accounts and filings of every entity, as well as the obligations specific to a property manager: the financial guarantee (garantie financière) that protects our clients' money, and the certifications of the funds we hold on their behalf (fonds mandants). You also cover the research tax credit (CIR) and tax.

2. Strategic topics (20%) :

  • Lead the finance team (4 people) and steer our external accountants and auditors on scope, calendar and fees.

  • Prepare the board deck and investor materials with the CFO, including for our 2027 fundraise, and bring a clear finance view to strategic decisions: acquisitions, growth versus capacity, cash allocation, pricing.

  • Drive our finance tools roadmap: selecting and rolling out an ERP (planned for late 2027), billing and payment tools, and automating data and reporting.

  • Pick up whatever else lands on finance: supplier negotiations, legal structure of our entities, equity events.

3. M&A (10%) : work with the other teams on financial analyses, billing, and the integration of the companies we acquire.

What success looks like after 12 months

  • The monthly close and reporting pack land on a fixed calendar in both countries, without escalation

  • Audits in France and Germany are signed on time and on fee; every entity's accounts are filed on time

  • Garantie financière and fonds mandants obligations are met with no gaps

  • The rolling business plan is the single reference for decisions, refreshed every month after close

  • The weekly cash forecast is trusted by the CEO and the board; collection has improved measurably

  • Every finance deliverable has a clear owner, and the German close runs locally

  • The ERP is selected and its implementation is on plan

What we offer

Benefits

  • Parental support: a gradual return at 80% for 4 weeks (paid at 100%), plus 5 extra days off per year when your child is sick.

  • Responsible commute leave: 1 extra paid day off per year (can be split into two half-days) to encourage low-carbon commuting.

  • Menstrual leave: 1 extra paid day off per month to manage painful periods.

  • Sport: access to Wellpass for affordable gym and sports.

  • Works council perks (Leeto): discounts on culture and leisure (cinema, museums, theme parks…).

  • Remote work: 2 days a week at the office.

  • Career support: weekly one-to-ones with your manager, 2 performance reviews a year, and an internal mobility policy.

  • A laptop and a work phone.

Practical information

  • Location: Paris 10th

  • Contract: permanent contract (CDI), full-time, cadre status on a forfait jours basis

  • Salary: €90k to €100k base, depending on experience

  • Start date: before July 2027


What we are looking for

You must have:

  • 7+ years in finance, including at least 2 years owning the close and audits of a multi-entity company, for example as Head of Finance, Finance Manager or Senior Financial Controller.

  • Hands-on experience of closing the books and running statutory audits in France: you know the French system (social charges, tax, statutory auditors).

  • Experience in a group with entities in other countries (not necessarily Germany).

  • You build and defend financial models (P&L, cash, headcount, churn) and can run a monthly business plan yourself.

  • You have managed a small team, and you still like doing some of the work yourself.

  • Fluent French and English, written and spoken.

You are:

  • Direct: you say when a number does not hold, including to the CEO.

  • Hands-on and structured: you turn open questions into plans with owners and deadlines.

  • Firm with suppliers: you manage auditors, accountants and vendors on scope, calendar and fees.

  • Autonomous and comfortable with change: you have worked in a growing company that needed structure.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with a German subsidiary or parent company, or speaking German.

  • Experience of acquisitions and their integration.

  • Experience in a regulated environment or with client funds (real estate, property management, fintech).

  • Experience of selecting or rolling out an ERP.

Our hiring process

1️⃣ A 30-minute phone call with Camille, our recruiter

2️⃣ A technical discussion with Krystal, our CFO, and Valent, our current Head of Finance (45 min, video call)

3️⃣ A case study to prepare and present to the CFO and Head Of Finance (45 min, video call)

4️⃣ A meeting with Raphaël, our CEO, and the team, at our office (1h)

5️⃣ Reference checks, then an offer

Good to know:

🕑 We do our best to get back to you quickly (within a week). Whether the answer is yes or no, you will receive an email from us, so remember to check your spam folder.

☝️ If you need any adjustments to take part in the interviews in the best conditions, let us know in your application or tell the recruitment team.

title: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
descriptionHtml:
About Us 

Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world. 

Hawk builds AI-powered financial crime detection (AML, transaction monitoring, and fraud prevention) for global tier-1 banks, payment processors, and high-growth fintechs. Because our platform analyzes real-time payment streams and sensitive financial data, security is not an administrative support function—it is our primary product promise.

We are looking for a technically grounded, hands-on CISO to own our global security posture end-to-end. This is a true player-coach leadership role. You will lead a dedicated team of four domain specialists while staying close enough to the technology to review cloud architecture, triage high-severity vulnerabilities, command critical incident responses first-hand, and debate technical security controls peer-to-peer with customer bank CISOs.

Why This Role Matters

  • Global Regulatory Scrutiny at Scale: We operate across key financial hubs including Germany, the UK, the US, Singapore, and a growing roster of international markets. With DORA enforceable across the EU and heightened ICT risk rules globally, our banking clients expect documented operational resilience, continuous testing, and verified controls across all jurisdictions.

  • Modern Attack Surfaces & Supply Chain Threats: Our multi-tenant and single-tenant cloud environments (AWS/GCP) process massive transaction throughput. Alongside defending against emerging supply chain vulnerabilities—from open-source dependencies to third-party build pipelines—you will need to deeply understand our AI approach and actively help harden our tooling, harnesses, and pipelines.

  • Enterprise Deal Velocity: Enterprise security reviews can either stall deals or close them. You will partner with our commercial teams to turn security questionnaires, risk mitigation, and architecture audits into enterprise trust and closed contracts.

Organizational Structure: The Four Domains

You will lead, mentor, and set technical direction for four specialized functional areas:

  1. Application Security: Secure SDLC, automated CI/CD security gates (SAST/DAST/SCA), software supply chain defense, secure coding standards, AI harnesses and pipeline hardening.

  2. Corporate Security: Zero Trust architecture, IAM/SSO, distributed endpoint defense (EDR/XDR), threat hunting, infrastructure access.

  3. Compliance & Governance: DORA implementation, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM), multi-jurisdiction regulatory audits, risk registry ownership.

  4. Data Protection: Solely dedicated to data protection: GDPR compliance, privacy governance, data subject rights, and statutory privacy regulatory requirements.

Core Accountabilities

1. Hands-On Technical Leadership, Engineering Integration & AI Hardening

  • Secure Coding Standards & SDLC: Establish and enforce secure coding baselines directly within engineering workflows. Ensure automated vulnerability scanning, SBOM tracking, and security gates are integrated into GitHub/GitLab CI/CD pipelines.

  • Software Supply Chain Defense: Protect build systems, dependencies, and deployment pipelines against supply chain tampering, compromised packages, and upstream vulnerabilities.

  • AI Tooling & Pipeline Hardening: Deeply understand our AI approach and work closely with engineering to harden our systems. Personally evaluate and implement protective mechanisms—including secure AI harnesses, container sandboxing, and runtime guardrails around AI tooling and workflows.

  • Vulnerability Lifecycle Management: Set strict remediation SLAs for CVEs and cloud misconfigurations. Directly arbitrate vulnerability severity, triage zero-days, and collaborate with engineering leads to ensure rapid remediation without stalling release velocity.

  • Zero Trust & Cloud Infrastructure: Architect and drive our group-wide Zero Trust roadmap across AWS and GCP environments, enforcing least-privilege IAM policies, network micro-segmentation, and secure developer access.

2. Commercial Trust & Customer Engagement

  • Peer-to-Peer Customer Dialogue: Act as the senior technical authority in enterprise sales cycles, engaging directly with bank CISOs, InfoSec panels, and procurement leads to validate Hawk's architecture, threat models, and operational controls.

  • Accelerating Enterprise Deal Velocity: Modernize vendor due diligence by replacing reactive security questionnaires with standardized evidence packages, continuous compliance portals, and pre-packaged architectural audits that win customer confidence quickly.

  • Converting Security into a Value Driver: Turn our robust security baseline into a core sales differentiator, helping commercial teams demonstrate to prospect banks why Hawk's defense posture makes us their lowest-risk vendor.

3. Risk Registry, Compliance & Governance Leadership

  • Company Risk Registry Ownership: Act as the executive owner of the company-wide Risk Registry. Go beyond cataloging risks: prioritize exposures dynamically, secure cross-functional executive buy-in to fund and execute mitigations, and transform risk management into concrete business enablement and revenue protection.

  • Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM): Oversee vendor risk tiering, supply chain vetting, and continuous monitoring for third-party vendors and cloud sub-processors, executed directly through the Compliance function.

  • Audit & Regulatory Leadership: Maintain existing ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II programs with zero major non-conformities across an expanding international perimeter.

  • DORA Implementation: Enforce end-to-end compliance with the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act—specifically ICT risk management, third-party vendor oversight, operational resilience testing, and ICT incident reporting.

  • Multi-Jurisdiction Alignment: Adapt policies proactively to meet global financial standards across the EU, UK, US, Singapore, and upcoming expansion markets.

  • Executive & Board Reporting: Translate technical cyber risks into clear business metrics (KRIs, risk heat maps, burn-down rates) for the CEO and Board of Directors.

4. Frontline Incident Response & Operational Resilience

  • First-Hand Incident Commander: Serve as the hands-on incident commander during Sev-1/Sev-2 security incidents. Lead technical investigations, root-cause analyses, log forensics, and technical debriefs directly alongside your team.

  • Breach Notification & External Escalation: Direct regulator, law enforcement, and client communications within mandatory statutory windows under GDPR and DORA guidelines.

  • Testing & Tabletop Drills: Design and execute technical red team engagements, threat-led penetration tests (TLPT), and crisis simulations with both technical engineers and the executive board.

12-Month Success Metrics:

  1. Commercial Velocity: Enterprise bank security assessments clear with zero high-severity blockers, accelerating enterprise contract closures.

  2. Proactive Risk Registry: The company risk registry is fully operationalized with executive buy-in, systematically driving down enterprise risk while supporting business expansion.

  3. Regulatory & Audit Record: DORA compliance program is operational; ISO 27001 and SOC 2 renew cleanly across all operating regions.

  4. Engineering & AI Hardening: Software supply chain security controls, secure coding standards, and AI harness guard rails are fully integrated into engineering CI/CD workflows.

  5. Resilient Team Operations: The four-person security team executes with high autonomy, defined KPIs, and high cross-functional trust across the company.

Candidate Profile:

  • Practitioner Foundations: Proven background as a hands-on security practitioner (e.g., former security engineer, AppSec specialist, cloud security architect, or technical penetration tester) who has advanced into security leadership.

  • Player-Coach Track Record: Demonstrated ability to manage and grow a small team of domain experts while personally reviewing technical configurations, auditing cloud policies, or investigating an alert.

  • Commercial & CISO-to-CISO Fluency: Experience debating architecture, supply chain controls, and threat postures directly with enterprise bank CISOs and security evaluation boards to clear deal roadblocks.

  • AI & Supply Chain Defense Fluency: Ability to quickly understand our AI architecture, implement hands-on controls to harden AI tooling (including AI harnesses and sandboxing), and protect CI/CD pipelines against software supply chain risks.

  • Risk Registry Execution: Demonstrated ability to maintain a living risk registry, articulate risk trade-offs to non-technical executives, and rally engineering and commercial buy-in to remediate risks.

  • FinTech & Regulated SaaS Background: Multi-year leadership experience in a B2B SaaS, FinTech, or banking platform handling sensitive financial or transactional data under regulatory oversight (e.g., DORA, ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR).

title: Clinical Lead, Women's Health
descriptionHtml:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

💜 The role

Women's bodies are different, yet medicine still treats them the same. Women get diagnosed about 4 years later than men on average across 700+ types of disease. In France, 51% of women say a health professional has played down their symptoms at least once.

We want to change that. We are building the health system women never had: one that listens to women, anticipates their needs at every stage of life instead of waiting for problems to appear, and gives them care they can trust. To do this, we combine the latest evidence, digital tools, AI and carefully selected health professionals with our strength as an insurer.

We are looking for a doctor who wants to do medicine differently: to build products that thousands of women use and that address their needs; to move care towards prevention; and to work every day with people who think differently, such as product managers, designers, engineers and marketers.

As our Clinical Lead for Women's Health, you make this clinically credible and effective. You own the clinical choices, and you are an essential and active contributor in the product team.

A few things to know before you apply

  • This is a clinical role inside a product team, at an early stage. You own the clinical choices and you build the product with project builder, engineers, designers, ... A good product combines many factors, and the clinical side is one of them. There is a lot to build, to test and to change, and not everything is proven yet. For example, we measure how much our services are used much better than the health outcomes they achieve: building that measurement, honestly, is part of the job.

  • You work outside the usual medical world. Most of your colleagues are not health professionals. You will confront perspectives, explain clinical constraints in simple words, listen to product and business constraints, and find solutions together. Decisions are discussed and made as a team.

  • It takes real time. We prefer 80% or more; at least 60% is possible.

What you will do

You will be the clinical lead of our Women's Health offer, and you will help turn it into a product that women use and trust.

  • Build the product with the team. Work closely with product managers, designers and engineers, and bring the clinical view early, when it shapes decisions, not at the end. With AI tools, you can also build simple things yourself, without knowing how to code.

  • Own the clinical choices. Define our clinical positions based on evidence, design protocols and care pathways, and hold a few clear, explained red lines. When something doesn't work, you help find a safe and relevant alternative.

  • Make our AI safe and accurate on women's health. Work with the product team on how Mo, our AI-powered health companion, handles women's health topics, and help evaluate and improve it.

  • Show the value for women. Help define how we measure the impact on women's health, using evidence-based tools and value-based healthcare principles.

  • Work with our Clinic team. Work hand in hand with Alan's doctors, midwives and other health professionals: help train and support them, and be the person they turn to for difficult cases.

  • Feed and endorse our medical communication. Make sure what we say about women's health is accurate and evidence-based, and help explain it in simple words. Over time, you may represent Alan on these topics.

What success looks like in 6 months

  • Product: you are a core member of the product team, and the first member journeys reflect your clinical input from the start.

  • Protocols in use: the clinical protocols and care pathways of our first women's health program are validated and applied by the Clinic team.

  • Clinic team: midwives and doctors on the program are trained on the protocols, clinical staffing is under way, and you supervise complex cases.

  • Health outcomes: the program's health outcomes are defined and tracked.

  • AI quality: you have helped us make sure our AI handles women's health safely and accurately.

What this role is not

  • Not a medical advisor or reviewer who comes in at the end, nor the person who decides alone.

  • Not the person who runs all the consultations: our midwives and doctors do that, and you design, pilot and supervise.

  • Not an expert on every topic: you bring in other health professionals when needed.

A dynamic, international community of health professionals

You don't work alone. You join Alan's health professionals community: a large network of doctors, midwives, psychologists and other clinicians in France, Spain, Belgium and Canada, and a small core team of Alaners, other clinical leads working on different health programs or services. It is a community with high standards, direct and caring feedback, and a lot of room to shape things.

Beyond Women's Health, you will:

  • Share your practice and learn from others through case reviews and community sessions;

  • Help set common standards across programs;

  • Help welcome, train and mentor new health professionals joining Alan;

  • Help other teams at Alan understand key health concepts, such as evidence-based care;

  • Over time, contribute to other health topics beyond Women's Health.

👀 Is it you we're looking for?

Must-haves

  • You are a gynecologist (OB-GYN) or a GP with solid training in women's health, for example a university diploma (DU or DIU) in gynecology, or several years of regular gynecological follow-up in your practice. You can come from private practice, a hospital, a clinic or a health tech company.

  • At least 5 years of post-residency experience, with solid clinical judgment and evidence-based prescribing.

  • Clinical experience across several areas of women's health, for example contraception, fertility, endometriosis, menopause or hormone treatments.

  • An open, pragmatic mindset: you enjoy working with non-medical teams, you make trade-offs when they are legitimate while defending evidence-based rigor, and you are curious about what AI and digital tools change in medicine.

  • Outcomes thinking: you care about the results that matter to patients compared with what care costs (value-based healthcare), and about prevention, not only treatment.

  • A great understanding of the French healthcare system.

  • Fluency in both French and English.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience training or supervising other health professionals is a plus, and a collaborative approach with midwives, dietitians, therapists, …

  • Experience in digital health, a start-up, a healthcare project or teleconsultation.

  • Experience writing or contributing to a clinical protocol or guideline.

🤝 How we work

  • Contract: you join Alan as an employee, ideally at 80% or more, and at least 60%. You can keep some clinical practice outside Alan.

  • Team: you are part of the Women's Health product team and of Alan's health professionals community.

  • Location: our headquarters are in Paris. You can be based abroad, as long as you speak French fluently and know the French healthcare system well.

  • Remote work: we offer remote work flexibility, but we value in-person collaboration.

🔄 What to expect from our recruitment process

  1. Application Review: we read your CV and application.

title: Constructor Student Labs
descriptionHtml:
Student Labs: Constructor Fabric Research Edition

Curious how AI is changing the way software is built? Want to explore it hands-on, guided by the researchers who work on it every day?

Constructor Tech and Constructor Labs, together with Constructor University, invite you to Student Labs: a 2-month educational research program for BSc and MSc students.

This edition is dedicated to Constructor Fabric, a shared AI and software platform. Fabric brings together reusable building blocks, common infrastructure and AI agents that help design, build and test software.

🚀 Why Constructor Fabric?

AI-native software platforms are one of the fastest-growing fields in tech, and few students get to study one from the inside. Student Labs gives you that chance. You explore open research questions on a platform in active development, learn current research methods, and build skills that are in high demand in industry and academia.

🔬 What you can research
 

AI that builds software

  • Domain-specific languages (DSL): how a formal language can describe software components so that AI can generate and regenerate them from specifications
  • Neurosymbolic models: combining neural networks with logic and rules, so that AI-generated code can be checked, not just produced
  • Rule extraction and fine-tuning: how to extract rules and knowledge from existing code and use them to adapt language models
  • World models: how AI systems build an internal model of their environment to understand, plan and predict
  • Formal verification: mathematical methods that prove software behaves as specified
  • Geometric models: using geometry to represent data and help AI models learn from it
  • Benchmarking: how to measure fairly whether one AI model or method is really better than another

Next-generation language models

  • Diffusion models for text: today’s LLMs write one token at a time, which makes them slow and prone to hallucinations. Diffusion models generate whole passages at once. Explore how to make them match and beat today’s models.
  • LLM security: how to host large language models securely when many users and organisations share the same system
💡 What you’ll experience
  • Explore an open research question that matches your level: beginner, intermediate or advanced
  • Learn from weekly mentoring sessions with Constructor researchers and engineers
  • Exchange ideas with other students, and study solo or in a pair
  • Present your results as a research report, prototype or research concept
🎓 Who can apply?
  • BSc and MSc students of Constructor University and our partner universities
  • Students with a strong interest in AI, LLMs, software engineering or research. Beginners are welcome!
👉 How it works
  1. Choose a topic from a curated list proposed by our researchers.
  2. Find your level. Topics are offered for beginner, intermediate and advanced students, so everyone can find one that fits.
  3. Study solo or in a pair, depending on the topic.
  4. Lead your own research and set your own schedule, with weekly guidance from your mentor.
  5. Present your results and receive feedback and a certificate of completion.
⭐ Why join?
  • Study a fast-growing field from inside a real AI platform
  • Learn from experts: weekly mentorship from researchers and engineers
  • Earn academic credit: depending on your university’s rules, the Labs can count towards your mandatory internship, earn you project credits, or become part of your thesis
  • Publish: strong results can be published, with you as an author
  • Build your research portfolio and receive a certificate
  • Next steps: thesis co-supervision, and you can apply for paid internships in the Constructor ecosystem (separate application)

📅 Duration: 2 months
📍 Format: remote, or hybrid in Bremen (DE), Sofia (BG) or Belgrade (RS)
🗓 Mentoring: weekly sessions with your mentor. About 10–15 hours a week; you set your own schedule.

Student Labs is an educational research program, not a job or an internship. Participation is unpaid and voluntary.

descriptionHtml:
About Baringa 

Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value. With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.

The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.

Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. Certified as a Great Place to Work around the world, Baringa has been recognised by the Financial Times in 22 categories of its UK Leading Management Consultants rankings, and by Forbes for four consecutive years as one of the World’s Best Management Consulting Firms.

Digital risk, cyber security and resilience are no longer cost centres – they are where value is won or lost

The Jaguar Land Rover cyber attack cost the company £196m and had a £1.9bn impact on the UK economy. The damage wasn't a data breach, it was an attack on the connected technology that runs the business. We protect the things which underpin our daily lives: energy, water, payments, banking, hospitals and critical public services – and the supply chains behind them.

We don't just advise clients; we design, build and stand up the frameworks, operating models and tooling that keep working long after we leave.

We're a specialist team scaling fast, and we're independent by design: no software to resell, no audit relationship to protect, so nothing shapes our advice except the problem in front of you.

We work in small teams of experienced consultants, so everyone has a voice. Quarterly promotion cycles and no quotas mean you are promoted when you are ready, not when a slot opens up.

We're looking for Consultants and Senior Consultants who want to be known for tackling our clients’ toughest problems in digital risk, security and resilience.

Our Digital Risk and Cyber practice is scaling fast, and we're looking for experienced Consultants who want to build and solve, not just advise

Our Digital Risk and Cyber (DRC) team helps clients secure the things that matter most – from their overall security strategy and operating model, to the specific technologies that drive value in their business. Our work is organised around two specialisms:

Digital Resilience: helping clients meet fast-moving security, resilience and regulatory obligations such as the Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF), the EU’s Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) and EU AI Act, and the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill.

Digital Trust: helping clients govern emerging technology and security risk, including AI, cloud and post-quantum cryptography.

We also build security into our clients' biggest change and transformation programmes, and run the regulatory and standards compliance work that underpins their operations.

We are independent by design. With no software to resell and no audit relationship to protect, our people can give a genuinely honest view – and be trusted advisors in the truest sense.

What you will be doing

  • Own the work: Take personal ownership of high-quality deliverables on complex engagements – shaping the approach, managing workstreams and making sure what we produce has real impact for the client.
  • Go deep: Build genuine depth in a specialism you care about, and become the go-to expert colleagues and clients rely on to get the hardest calls right.
  • Solve, don't just advise: Design frameworks, build operating models and stand up tooling that clients actually use – using AI to compress high-volume work, so your time is spent on the judgement.
  • Be the critical friend: Advise CISOs and their teams directly across financial services, energy, government and critical national infrastructure – balancing technical depth, commercial understanding and the relationships that make advice land.
  • Help build the business: Grow your network and profile, contribute to new and evolving propositions, put yourself forward for the right opportunities, and spot ways to create more value for clients.
  • Grow – and grow others: Own your development, and support and coach the people around you to be at their best. 

Your skills and experience  

We care more about the shape of your experience than a checklist. If most of the following sound like you, we'd love to hear from you:

  • Digital risk and cyber experience: a track record in digital risk, cyber security or resilience, whether gained in consulting or in-house, and a genuine passion for the field.
  • Frameworks and standards: working knowledge of the standards and frameworks that shape our work, for example NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and the regulatory agenda, for example the EU AI Act, DORA, the UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill and CAF.
  • Delivery and client craft: experience delivering in demanding, client-facing environments (programme or project delivery, risk assessments, governance and assurance), with the communication skills to engage anyone from a technology team to the board.
  • Technology and AI literacy: fluency in, or real curiosity about, using AI to deliver – compressing high-volume work such as regulatory mapping, evidence review and maturity scoring – and advising clients on securing and governing it.
  • Experience in one or more of our domains: meaningful experience in at least one area we operate in, particularly: OT/ICS security, CAF, AI security and governance, post-quantum and cryptographic agility, operational resilience, strategy and operating model, supply chain risk, security architecture, crisis management and DevSecOps. 

Bonus Points

  • Certifications: CISSP, ISO, AI regulation and other certifications are a plus, but don’t replace real world experience.
  • Building tooling and automation: hands-on with building, for example agentic AI, Power BI, Power Apps, risk quantification models or digital twins. 

What a career at Baringa will give you 


Putting People First.

Baringa is a People First company and wellbeing is at the forefront of our culture. We recognise the importance of work-life balance and flexible working and provide our staff amazing benefits. Some of these benefits include: 

  • Generous Annual Leave Policy: We recognise everyone needs a well-deserved break. We provide our employees with 5 weeks of annual leave, fully available at the start of each year. In addition to this, we have introduced our 5-Year Recharge benefit which allows all employees an additional 2 weeks of paid leave after 5 years continuous service. 
  • Flexible Working: We know that the ‘ideal’ work-life balance will vary from person to person and change at different stages of our working lives. To accommodate this, we have implemented a hybrid working policy and introduced more flexibility around taking unpaid leave.

  • Profit Share Scheme: All employees participate in the Baringa Group Profit Share Scheme so everyone has a stake in the company’s success. 

Diversity and Inclusion

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We believe that creating an environment where everyone feels a sense of belonging is central to our culture and that diversity is paramount to driving creativity, innovation, and value for our clients and for our people. 

An award-winning workplace

title: Customer Marketing Manager, EMEA
descriptionHtml:
Horizon3.ai is seeking a customer-focused, data-driven Customer Marketing Manager to build engagement, adoption, retention, expansion, and advocacy across our EMEA customer base. You will create programs that help customers realize more value from Horizon3, strengthen customer relationships, and turn successful outcomes into credible customer proof.

This role brings together customer lifecycle marketing and customer advocacy. You will develop regional customer communications and campaigns while building a repeatable advocacy engine across customer stories, references, third-party reviews, speakers, and other strategic opportunities. You will work closely with Customer Success, Sales, Product Marketing, Product, and the broader Marketing team to turn customer needs and business priorities into useful, measurable programs.

The ideal candidate is both a strategic planner and a hands-on operator. You can build trust with customers, coordinate complex projects across teams and markets, use data to improve programs, and make it straightforward for customers to participate.

What you will do

Customer lifecycle marketing

  • Plan and execute customer marketing programs across onboarding, activation, adoption, engagement, retention, renewal support, and expansion.

  • Define customer segments, lifecycle stages, journey maps, messaging, and campaign playbooks that can be adapted for EMEA audiences.

  • Partner with Customer Success and Customer Enablement to promote onboarding, education, product engagement, and other programs that help customers achieve meaningful outcomes.

  • Develop proactive re-engagement programs for at-risk or under-engaged accounts using customer health, product usage, support, engagement, and renewal signals.

  • Create signal-based campaigns tied to customer needs, product usage, account changes, renewal timing, and expansion fit. Route qualified opportunities to the appropriate Customer Success Managers and account executives.

  • Partner with Product Marketing and Product to translate customer feedback into product communications, release messaging, educational content, and lifecycle campaigns.

  • Equip Sales and Customer Success with customer-centric messaging, adoption resources, executive business review materials, playbooks, and clear follow-up paths.

Customer advocacy and proof

  • Build and maintain a pipeline of EMEA customer advocates based on customer outcomes, engagement, use cases, and willingness to participate.

  • Partner with Customer Success Managers and account teams to identify customers for case studies, video testimonials, customer quotes, social content, references, and events.

  • Manage customer participation from outreach through briefing, approvals, production, publication, and follow-up. Coordinate logo rights, quotes, and other customer permissions with the appropriate internal teams.

  • Create and manage a practical customer reference program that supports sales opportunities, renewals, expansions, and strategic marketing needs. Maintain an organized reference pool and manage requests from intake and matching through scheduling, follow-up, and recognition.

  • Own day-to-day Peerbound administration and adoption, including customer profiles, advocacy requests, reference activity, permissions, and reporting. Help Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success use the platform consistently and make fuller use of its capabilities.

  • Develop and execute a focused third-party review strategy across relevant platforms, such as G2 and Gartner Peer Insights. Coordinate authentic customer outreach and track review volume, ratings, sentiment, category placement, competitor positioning, and progress against award criteria.

  • Maintain a qualified pipeline of customer speakers for webinars, user groups, events, panels, and other marketing programs. Confirm speakers early enough to include them in event promotions, landing pages, emails, and social campaigns, and manage briefing, preparation, logistics, approvals, and follow-up.

  • Own the customer invitation process for Customer Advisory Board opportunities and support customer recruitment for analyst interviews, research, awards, and other strategic initiatives.

  • Work with Content, Product Marketing, Social, Events, Communications, Analyst Relations, and Creative to elevate customers alongside the Horizon3.ai brand and turn customer outcomes into reusable marketing assets.

Program operations and measurement

  • Build annual and quarterly customer marketing plans for EMEA, manage budgets and resources, and lead cross-functional execution.

  • Work with Marketing Operations, Revenue Operations, and Customer Success Operations to improve segmentation, data quality, trigger detection, nurture, automation, attribution, and reporting.

  • Establish dashboards and operating rhythms that connect program engagement to adoption, customer advocacy, renewal health, retention, expansion pipeline, and influenced revenue.

  • Define success measures, analyze results, identify opportunities to improve, and iterate on program strategy, messaging, and execution.

  • Communicate timelines, owners, status, risks, and next steps clearly across teams. Create practical templates, trackers, and workflows that make customer marketing easier to execute and scale.

What you bring

  • 7+ years of marketing experience, including 3+ years in customer marketing, lifecycle marketing, customer advocacy, customer success enablement, or a related discipline.

  • Experience building customer journeys and programs across adoption, engagement, retention, renewal, expansion, or advocacy.

  • A track record of managing customer stories, references, reviews, speakers, or other advocacy programs, ideally alongside lifecycle marketing responsibilities.

  • Strong relationship-building skills and confidence communicating with customers and internal stakeholders.

  • Experience partnering with Customer Success, Sales, Product Marketing, Product, Marketing Operations, and Revenue Operations.

  • Strong project management and follow-through, with the ability to manage multiple programs and deadlines across teams and markets.

  • Analytical and operational skills, including the ability to connect customer behavior and program performance to business outcomes.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the judgment to represent customer perspectives accurately and authentically.

  • Familiarity with customer advocacy, reference, review, CRM, or marketing automation platforms. Peerbound experience is a plus.

  • Understanding of B2B SaaS or cybersecurity customer environments is a plus.

  • Ability to work effectively across EMEA markets and time zones. Additional language skills are a plus.

How success is measured

  • Lifecycle program engagement and contribution to customer adoption, retention, renewal health, and expansion.

  • Growth and health of the EMEA customer advocate and reference pool, including references fulfilled and customer participation.

  • Customer proof produced, including case studies, videos, quotes, approved logos, and social or event participation.

  • Customer speakers confirmed in time to support event and webinar promotion.

  • Peerbound adoption, data quality, and program activity.

  • Review volume, ratings, sentiment, and progress against award criteria.

  • Customer experience and internal stakeholder satisfaction.
