title: Group Data Protection Officer
descriptionHtml:
Group Data Protection Officer | M-KOPA

Remote (covering Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa and the UK)

You're the lawyer people call when a data question has no easy answer. You're accomplished. You're respected. You're probably even happy. But is your work protecting millions of people who are trusting a formal financial service with their personal information for the very first time?

That is the question at the heart of this role.

The trust you'd be protecting

M-KOPA now serves 10 million customers, up from 5 million in 2024, and has unlocked $2+ billion in credit. 86% of our customers report an improved quality of life, 70% use our products to earn an income, and 55% are accessing products and services for the first time. Behind them stand 2,300+ employees and 35,000 agents. Every one of those customers has handed us personal information, and they did it because they believed we would handle it with care. Across Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Uganda and the UK, that belief is held under six different sets of rules, each with its own expectations about consent, retention, cross-border transfers and what happens when something goes wrong. The customers who benefit most from what we build are often the ones with the least room to absorb a mistake with their data, and that is the standard this role exists to hold.

Why this timing matters

You may have seen us advertising several roles across Legal, Risk and Compliance. That is deliberate, not random. We've moved from 5 million customers to 7 million, and we are now building beyond 10 million. The legal, risk and privacy foundations have to be laid ahead of that growth, not scrambled together after it. New markets, new products and new partners all arrive with new data questions. Joining now means shaping the privacy programme while its biggest chapters are still ahead of it.

What makes this different

In many organisations, the data protection officer reviews things at the end of the process. Here, the role reaches the whole group. Your current role: one jurisdiction, one regime. This role: six markets, one customer promise.

You would report day to day to the Chief Legal, Risk and Compliance Officer, with reporting to the CEO and the Board as well. Your recommendations on strategy and implementation go to the people who run the company, and they shape how the business executes. Your work also connects directly to our mission. Financial inclusion only works if the people we serve can trust us with what they share, and you would be one of the people who keeps that trust earned. Because the role spans the whole group, you would also see patterns that no single market team can: where the same gap appears in several places, and where one fix can protect every customer at once.

What you'll bring

  • Qualified lawyer with extensive, progressive experience in data protection and privacy compliance, including running privacy operations end to end: data protection impact assessments, transfer impact assessments, vendor assessments and risk management.

  • Detailed command of data protection law across our six markets, paired with a sound understanding of information systems, data processing operations and security needs, so you can challenge the architecture as confidently as the contract.

  • Demonstrable experience developing policies, guidelines and template clauses for the processing of personal data, and proficiency in using AI tools responsibly to support privacy research, compliance work and risk assessment.

A recognised privacy or security certification (CIPP, CIPT, or ISO 27001 or 27701 implementer or auditor) is an added advantage. It is not a gate.

What you'll actually do

  • Run the programme and fix what you find. Lead remediation and data audits, conduct DPIAs, identify where we are partially or fully non-compliant, and put it right across all six markets, while keeping the records of processing that prove it.

  • Build the tools everyone else uses. Write the guidelines, template clauses and contracts that govern how partners, suppliers and vendors handle personal information, and support the privacy software, incident response and breach notification procedures behind them.

  • Turn the law into culture. Design training and internal communications for staff, run awareness for third parties, and support due diligence, certification, audits and new-market expansion, so data protection is something every team does rather than something Legal does to them.

The reality check

This role is demanding. You will hold six regimes in your head at once, advise colleagues who would rather hear a different answer, and move a business forward with clear, plain-English advice. It is an onsite role, and your calendar will hold the strategic and the urgent in the same week: a policy redesign on Monday, a vendor assessment on Wednesday, a breach notification drill on Friday. The work rewards people who like building systems that still work when nobody is watching. You're probably ready for exactly this.

Ready to build the privacy standard 10 million customers can rely on?

If you read the question at the top of this page and felt something, that is probably the signal. Let's talk.

Why M-KOPA?

At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility.

Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com.

Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya.

Important Notice

M-KOPA is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer committed to assembling a diverse, broadly trained staff. Women, minorities, and people with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply.

M-KOPA explicitly prohibits the use of Forced or Child Labour and respects the rights of its employees to agree to terms and conditions of employment voluntarily, without coercion, and freely terminate their employment on appropriate notice. M-KOPA shall ensure that its Employees are of legal working age and shall comply with local laws for youth employment or student work, such as internships or apprenticeships. 

M-KOPA does not collect/charge any money as a pre-employment or post-employment requirement. This means that we never ask for ‘recruitment fees’, ‘processing fees’, ‘interview fees’, or any other kind of money in exchange for offer letters or interviews at any time during the hiring process.

Applications for this position will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisting and interviews will take place at any stage during the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a suitable candidate is selected before the advertised closing date.

If your application is successful M-KOPA undertakes pre-employment background checks as part of its recruitment process, these include; criminal records, identification verification, academic qualifications, employment dates and employer references.

title: Group Product Manager (m/w/d) / Team Lead Product
descriptionHtml:
Einleitung

Bei Peter Park ist "Product" nicht einfach nur ein Unternehmensbereich. Hier trifft alles aufeinander: Wohin wir als Unternehmen wollen, was wir verkaufen, wie wir wachsen, was unsere Kunden erleben. Als Group Product Manager verantwortest du eine Product Area im Produktmanagement, führst ein Team von Product Managern und arbeitest täglich mit einem breiten Stakeholder-Feld zusammen. Wenn du wirklich gestalten und führen willst, ist das die richtige Stelle.

Was ist Deine Aufgabe?

  • People Leadership, Coaching & Culture: Du hast die volle disziplinarische Verantwortung für ein Team von 2–3 Product Managern und prägst die Teamkultur mit dem Ziel, wachsende Eigenverantwortung und Empowerment im Team zu entwickeln.

  • Produktstrategie & Alignment: Du entwickelst und verantwortest die Strategie für deine Product Area und stellst das kontinuierliche Alignment mit unseren Unternehmenszielen sicher. Du managst den Produktlebenszyklus und pflegst den Product Governance Prozess – schnell liefern, ohne Qualität zu opfern.

  • Business Impact & Markt: Du steuerst Ressourcen für maximalen Impact und bewertest und verbesserst kontinuierlich die Kundenzufriedenheit auf Area-Ebene. Dafür hast du Markttrends und den Wettbewerb stets im Blick.

  • Stakeholder-Management: Du hältst für deine Product Area die Fäden zusammen und hast stets das große Ganze im Blick. Dabei kommunizierst du sicher mit unterschiedlichen Unternehmensbereichen und Managementebenen.

Deine Fähigkeiten:

  • Du bringst 7+ Jahre relevante Erfahrung als Senior PM, Lead PM oder Team Lead im Product Management mit – idealerweise in einem schnellwachsenden Start-up, Scale-up, SaaS- oder IoT-Umfeld.

  • Du hast über 1,5 Jahre Erfahrung in der disziplinarischen Führung.

  • Du hast eigenständig eine Produktstrategie auf Area-Ebene entwickelt und verantwortet – inkl. Roadmap-Planung.

  • Du arbeitest sicher mit agilen Methoden und bist vertraut mit Outcome-Metriken und datenbasierter Entscheidungsfindung.

  • Du verfügst über exzellente Kommunikationsfähigkeiten für unterschiedliche Zielgruppen und eine ausgeprägte Fähigkeit zur internen Kollaboration.

  • Du denkst unternehmerisch, übernimmst Ownership für komplexe Themen und verlierst dabei nie das große Ganze aus dem Blick.

  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und verfügst über gute Englischkenntnisse.

Work Setup:

  • 40 Stunden pro Woche (Vertrauensbasis)

  • Homeoffice Policy: 3 Tage im Office / 2 Tage remote

  • Unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag

  • Arbeitsort: München

  • Team: 6 Kolleg:innen

Welche Vorteile bietet mir Peter Park?

So sieht Dein Arbeitsalltag bei uns aus

  • Arbeiten mit Bergblick: Unser Büro in der Neuen Balan bietet mehr als nur moderne Ausstattung: Von der Dachterrasse aus genießt Du ein Alpenpanorama, im Sommer wird gemeinsam gegrillt, und unsere Teamevents sorgen für gute Stimmung.

  • Teamgeist und Impact-Kultur: Bei uns zählt Deine Stimme! Wir leben flache Hierarchien und eine Kultur des "Du" vom ersten Tag an. Das bedeutet: kurze Entscheidungswege, direkter Austausch mit allen Ebenen und ein Team, das Dich aktiv unterstützt. Deine Ideen sind hier nicht nur willkommen, sondern werden gehört.

  • Freiraum für Deine Ideen: Du übernimmst Verantwortung und kannst Deine Ideen aktiv einbringen. Wir fördern Deine Entwicklung – mit echtem Vertrauen in Deine Fähigkeiten.

title: Growth Manager Revenue Operations (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
1KOMMA5°

Bei 1KOMMA5° verfolgen wir eine Vision: Living on wind and sunlight forever for free. Dafür bauen wir mit Heartbeat AI das Energiesystem der Zukunft. Bist du dabei?
Wir bringen regionales Handwerk und skalierbare Software zusammen: Solar, Speicher, Wärmepumpe und E-Mobilität denken wir nicht einzeln, sondern steuern sie als intelligentes, integriertes Gesamtsystem in unserem virtuellen Kraftwerk. Direkt verbunden mit dem Strommarkt – in Echtzeit, vollautomatisiert. So wird Energie dann genutzt, wenn sie erneuerbar verfügbar und besonders günstig ist. Bis 2030 wollen wir 1,5 Millionen Haushalte auf erneuerbare Energien umstellen. Über 3.000 Menschen arbeiten jeden Tag daran, an mehr als 80 Standorten weltweit, von Finnland bis Australien.

Du willst Verantwortung übernehmen und Lösungen bauen, die wirklich zählen? Bewirb dich jetzt und gestalte mit uns die Energiewelt von morgen.

Deine Position

  • Jeden Monat fragen Tausende Haushalte bei uns eine Beratung für Solar, Wärmepumpe oder Heartbeat AI an. Bis zur Unterschrift ist es ein ganz schöner Weg: Inside Sales, über 40 Standorte, Kalender, CRM und jede Menge Übergaben per Hand. Mal läuft die Pipeline richtig gut, mal hakt es an mehreren Stellen gleichzeitig
  • Da setzt du an. Du machst diesen Weg schneller, sauberer und messbar, und du baust dafür selbst: Systeme, Prozesse und Auswertungen, die auch dann noch halten, wenn wir weiter wachsen
  • Du wirst Teil unseres kleinen RevOps-Teams in Growth. Wir sind so etwas wie das Schweizer Taschenmesser im Haus: Mal löschen wir Brände, mal bauen wir Dinge, die dauerhaft laufen. Wir sind über die ganze Customer Journey unterwegs und sitzen mit Sales, Marketing und Tech am Tisch, und die wollen nicht immer dasselbe. Wir halten es pragmatisch. Uns interessiert vor allem, ob es fürs Business und für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden wirklich was bringt

Was du verantwortest

  • Mehrere Journey Funnel-Stufen und die wichtigsten Kennzahlen liegen bei dir. Du behältst die Hebel im Blick, findest heraus, wo und warum es hakt, baust die Lösung und testest sie an ein, zwei Standorten. Du skalierst funktionierende Lösungen in alle Märkte
  • Je nach Profil arbeitest du mehr in der Breite oder mehr in der Tiefe. Dein Schwerpunkt liegt entweder auf Lead Routing, Scoring, Qualifizierung und unserem Kontakt- und Terminsystem oder auf dem Weg vom qualifizierten Lead zum Angebot.
  • Dazu gehören die Systeme dahinter: die Dashboards, mit denen gesteuert wird, die Prozesse und Automatisierungen, die alles am Laufen halten, und die Daten, auf denen es aufbaut
  • Deine Lösungen baust du selbst, bringst sie in den operativen Betrieb und rollst sie aus. Wo es nötig ist, arbeitest du dabei mit unseren Tech-Teams zusammen

Was du konkret machst

  • Steuerung aufbauen: Looker-Dashboards, Alerts und SLAs, mit denen Vertriebsleitungen in der Zentrale und an den Standorten jede Woche arbeiten
  • Übergaben automatisieren: Routing, Terminvergabe, die Übergabe von Inside Sales an die Standorte und den Umgang mit No-Shows und Dubletten
  • AI-Workflows selbst bauen: Prototypen in Windmill oder n8n, die du gemeinsam mit MarTech und Tech live bringst
  • Für saubere Daten sorgen: Felddefinitionen, Pflichtfelder, regelmäßige Datenpflege und Source-of-Truth-Regeln in unserem CRM (Zoho)
  • Piloten sauber aufsetzen: Hypothese, ein bis zwei Standorte, gemessenes Ergebnis und am Ende die Entscheidung, ob ausgerollt wird
  • Einen Backlog an Optimierungsmaßnahmen aufbauen: Call-Transkripte, Pipeline- und Standortdaten werden zu einer priorisierten Liste, was als Nächstes gebaut wird
  • Teams mitnehmen und enablen: Mit Dokumentation, Trainings und Rollouts sorgst du dafür, dass Standortleitungen, Inside Sales und Vertrieb deine Systeme auch nutzen

Damit arbeitest du unter anderem: Zoho CRM, Looker, Windmill, n8n, Heyflow, Calendly, Aircall, ActiveCampaign, Telli, Google Workspace

Dein Profil

  • Du hast 1-2+ Jahre oder mehr Erfahrung in RevOps, Sales Ops, GTM Engineering oder einer vergleichbaren Rolle. Dort hast du eine Funnel-Kennzahl wirklich verantwortet und nicht nur reported
  • Du weißt, wie ein Sales Funnel funktioniert, von Lead über Qualifizierung, Deal und Angebot bis zum Upsell. Und du weißt, was an jeder Stelle die Conversion und Cycle Time treibt
  • Du hast KPIs, Automatisierungen oder AI-Workflows selbst aufgebaut und live gebracht, etwa mit Windmill, n8n, Make, Python, Claude etc. Und sie werden im Alltag tatsächlich skaliert genutzt
  • Deine Dashboards baust du selbst, in Looker, Power BI, Tableau oder einem ähnlichen Tool. Dass die Daten am Anfang unsauber sind, schreckt dich nicht ab
  • Du kennst dich mit CRM-Systemen aus (Zoho oder ähnliche), vom Datenmodell über Workflows bis zu Integrationen
  • Du arbeitest gern eng mit Tech, Sales und Marketing zusammen und sprichst die Sprache aller drei. Technische Trade-offs übersetzt du in Business-Entscheidungen und kommerzielle Prioritäten in technische Anforderungen, ohne dass jemand vermitteln muss
  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und Englisch, in Wort und Schrift

Das ist ein Plus

  • Du hast schon mit einer Vertriebsorganisation mit Standorten oder Außendienst gearbeitet, nicht nur aus der Zentrale heraus
  • Du hast Lead Management schon praktisch umgesetzt: Scoring, Routing, Nurturing, Terminvergabe etc
  • Du hast erste Agents, z.B. extern Voice AI oder Conversational Agents oder interne Effizienz-Automatisierungen schon live gebracht
  • Du hast Erfahrung mit dem B2C-Geschäft und mit hochpreisigen Produkten, etwa Energie, Solar, Hausmodernisierung oder Automotive

Benefits

  • Du hast die Möglichkeit in unseren brandneuen Büros in der Hamburger Innenstadt & Berlin zu arbeiten und hybrid
  • Nutze dein technisches Equipment auch abseits der Arbeit in deiner Freizeit
  • Du bist Teil eines schnell wachsenden Unternehmens mit viel Entwicklungspotenzi al, wo du eigenständig etwas aufbauen kannst und deinen Impact spürst
  • Bewege dich in flachen Hierarchien, übernimm schon während deiner Einarbeitung Verantwortung und arbeite direkt mit Teilen des Managements zusammen
  • Mit deiner Arbeit unterstützt du den Megatrend “Energie- und Mobilitätswende” und leistest einen konkreten Beitrag zum nachhaltigen Umbau unserer Energie-Infrastruktur
  • Sei aktiv und nutze das Angebot von über 7.600 Sportpartnern mit dem EGYM-Wellpass
  • Ob Citybike oder E-Bike – mit unserem Jobrad-Leasing bleibst du flexibel und bist umweltfreundlich unterwegs
  • Profitiere von Benefits & Rabatten durch Futurebens

title: Growth Manager / Senior Growth Manager - Software (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Du bist Hunter mit Strategie-Gen: Du jagst Wachstumschancen, denkst in Portfolios statt in Einzelprojekten und in Kundenbeziehungen statt in Einzelabschlüssen – und du machst andere erfolgreich? Dann gestalte mit uns, womit und wie die Coduct Solutions im deutschsprachigen Mittelstand wächst.

Coduct Group in 30 Sekunden

Wir modernisieren IT für Unternehmen, die mit Software Geld verdienen oder ihre Prozesse digitalisieren: Cloud-Migration, Daten & KI, individuelle Software und Betrieb. Dazu gehören unser Marke CODE LEAP in Vietnam für das Software Engineering, unsere Marke ainavio mit einer SaaS-Plattform für Produktinformationsmanagement und unser Geschäft als Microsoft CSP-Partner. Wir sind dreifach zertifizierter Microsoft Solutions Partner und arbeiten u. a. für JTL, Netze BW, Schleupen und Galeria.

Für die nächste Wachstumsphase haben wir die Funktion Growth gegründet. Ein VP Growth plant das Wachstum und befähigt Marketing und Vertrieb, es zu realisieren. Du wirst das erste Teammitglied an seiner Seite.

Deine Mission

Ein Portfolio und eine Roadmap bauen, mit denen Coduct nachhaltig wächst – und Marketing und Vertrieb so ausstatten, dass sie damit gewinnen.

Drei Prinzipien, die du mit uns umsetzt

Land & Expand

  • Kunden starten mit einem klaren, risikoarmen Einstiegsangebot – und wachsen über definierte Ausbaupfade in Projekte, Managed Services, Lizenzen und SaaS. Aus Aufträgen werden langfristige Kundenbeziehungen.

Balance Volumen & Premium

  • Standardisierte Volumenangebote sorgen für Skalierung und wiederkehrende Umsätze, individuelle Premiumleistungen für Differenzierung und Marge. Du gestaltest den Mix so, dass sich beide Welten verstärken.

Hunting

  • Wachstum wartet nicht. Du spürst Chancen aktiv auf – Segmente, Partner, Großchancen – und bringst sie gemeinsam mit dem Vertrieb zum Abschluss. Dein Erfolg zeigt sich in Umsatz und EBIT – und in deiner variablen Vergütung.

Deine ersten 12 Monate

Monat 1–3

Monat 4–6

Das bringst du mit

Du passt zu uns, wenn …

  • du als Hunter neue Wachstumschancen jagst – und sie mit dem Vertrieb zum Abschluss bringst

  • du dich gern an Ergebnissen messen lässt – an KPIs, Umsatz und EBIT

Eher nicht, wenn …

Das bekommst du

title: Hardware-Aware Model Optimisation - Member of Technical Staff
descriptionHtml:
About Us

We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.

Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next.

The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.

Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.

Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor.

In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence.

We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

Callosum believes that the next generation of AI systems will emerge from models and hardware being optimised together. Today's model architectures have largely evolved around the capabilities of conventional GPUs, leaving significant opportunities unexplored as new accelerator architectures emerge. We are building infrastructure that allows models to be adapted to different computational substrates, rather than treating them as fixed algorithms that hardware must accommodate.

This role explores how model architectures and inference algorithms can be adapted to exploit heterogeneous hardware, creating specialised variants with different trade-offs between capability, latency, and cost. You will investigate transformations spanning numerics, sparsity, model structure, memory, and execution, alongside new algorithms designed around emerging accelerators. A central part of the work is developing automated approaches to these adaptations and rigorous evaluations that establish when the resulting models offer meaningful advantages.

What You'll Build

  • Develop hardware-aware transformations that adapt models to different accelerator architectures and execution environments.

  • Explore numerical, structural, and memory-related optimisations to create model variants with different capability, latency, and cost trade-offs.

  • Investigate new inference algorithms, including speculative decoding, designed to exploit heterogeneous computational resources.

  • Develop automated methods for discovering, characterising, and optimising hardware-specialised model variants.

  • Build evaluation methods that measure model quality and establish the trade-offs introduced by hardware-aware adaptations.

What Sets You Apart

  • Deep understanding of modern LLM architectures, including attention mechanisms, model structure, and their implications for inference.

  • Experience in model architecture research, efficient inference, or hardware-aware machine learning.

  • Familiarity with a range of architectures, such as mixture-of-experts, diffusion, JEPA, or alternative attention mechanisms.

  • Strong intuition for the interactions between model capability, numerical behaviour, memory requirements, and execution efficiency.

  • Experience designing rigorous experiments to assess model quality, efficiency, and the effects of architectural modifications.

What We Offer

  • Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience

  • Equity & Ownership

  • Private healthcare

  • We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

  • We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell us

We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome, and believe in equal opportunities for all.

title: Harness Research Engineer | 36labs
descriptionHtml:
Role: Harness Research Engineer

Company: 36 Labs

Location: London, in the office four days a week (Baker Street now, moving to Primrose Hill within a couple of months). London-based candidates only. No visa sponsorship is available at the moment.

Job Type: Full-time

About 36 Labs

36 Labs is an applied AI research firm in London. It is teaching models what captures human attention on social media, and it starts with creativity. The founders see a creative process as a tree of decisions. LLMs are poor at that, and they are poor at explaining why a creative choice was made.

The product is a harness that sits over any frontier model, especially video generation models. An autonomous marketing service runs on it, from ideation to generation to distribution. The content goes to real audiences, and the results feed a data loop that improves the harness. Clients so far are mainly music companies, including Sony, Warner and Universal. Marketing is a proof of concept. The company does not see itself as a marketing business.

The company is profitable and is closing its first seed round in the next couple of weeks. V3 of the harness is being released internally, and the scope of work is large. The founders are sure of the direction. They need someone to own delivery. Today only one or two people can work on the harness, so you would be one of the first. This is a new role, created by the next stage of growth.

The stack is Python, TypeScript, Postgres, LLM and generative model APIs, and open-weight models.

What you are expected to do:

  • Continue developing the harness, including the V3 release.

  • Take ownership of delivering the harness. The direction is set, and getting it built is your job.

  • Build and run benchmarks and evals.

  • Own the evaluation pipeline for the harness, across text, video and images.

  • Turn fuzzy quality questions into validated evaluation models for open-ended agent tasks.

What you need to succeed:

Experience

  • You have 4+ years of experience and have owned something before, from start to finish.

  • You are a hands-on engineer in the AI-native era and can work independently.

  • Agents and evals are the company's main priorities. You have shipped evals for outputs that cannot be tracked automatically, such as open-ended, non-numerical tasks.

  • Ideally you have shipped an agent system with real users and workloads. It relies on models, calls tools and acts on the results of planning steps. A basic chat interface with retrieval behind it is not enough, and neither is agent work limited to data extraction.

  • You can work from the London office four days a week and do not need visa sponsorship right now. A visa valid until next June, for example, is fine. A month's notice is fine too. Starting earlier is preferred, though November or December is acceptable.

Nice to have

  • A degree in computer science, engineering, maths, stats or similar. An MSc or PhD is great. With a BSc only, you need to be really good. The university matters less than what you have built.

  • Experience with multimodal models or post-training.

  • A background in applied generative media or creative companies, such as Fal.

  • Projects beyond university or your day job, and a habit of keeping up with new stacks, models and practices.

How you work

  • You have high agency. You take the lead and need little hand-holding.

  • You do things first and ask forgiveness later, and you are open to being disagreed with.

  • You explain your ideas clearly to the team and leave your ego at the door.

What you get:

  • Real ownership. You would own the delivery of the harness, which only one or two colleagues can work on today.

  • Work on a problem few other companies are tackling. The team believes that solving creativity in LLMs would solve the human attention economy, and they see a very high ceiling.

  • Clients such as Sony, Warner and Universal.

  • Fast learning at a seed-stage company, which is also a strong line on a CV.

  • Room to grow into a more senior role. The CTO is expected to step back from the code over the long term.

  • A pace that is extremely fast and comes without stability. The team sees that as a good thing, and we want you to know it upfront.

How to apply

Send your LinkedIn profile or CV, with a short note on the projects you are proudest of, to your contact at the agency. Use the subject line "Harness Research Engineer, 36 Labs". The process starts with a short pre-screen call with the agency. Next comes a conversation with Benedict, head of operations, then a technical interview of about 30 minutes with the CTO, then a take-home assessment. If the team is torn between strong candidates, there may be a final session on-site in the office.

descriptionHtml:

Taptap Send Business is early and growing fast. Businesses are already using us to pay people and suppliers across emerging markets, and we are launching a wider set of products and geographies. Every launch is a new promise to a business customer whose payroll, suppliers and cash flow depend on us getting it right.

This role reports to the Director of Business Operations and owns the service our business customers get. You will be given high agency and high autonomy, working across Product, Data, Engineering and Compliance to build and run best-in-class support for a product line that is growing fast.

The outcome you will drive

Responsibilities

  • Set the standard our BPO partners are held to — playbooks, QA, KPIs — and hold the performance bar high

  • Structure complex and ambiguous problems by conducting ad hoc analysis

  • Act as Product Ops for the Business line: turn what customers tell us into evidenced product priorities, and get them built

  • Own support for each new launch, from readiness through to a steady, automated state

Requirements

  • 5-7+ years of high-performing experience in a fast pace, analytical environment

  • B2B account management, customer success or business operations for a business/SME product is what we are looking for, you know what business customers expect and what it takes to deliver it

A BizOps role at Taptap Send is a super Individual Contributor. For your topic you are the single threaded owner, the analyst, the product manager, the engineer and the operations lead. In practice you don’t wait for others, you leverage AI to get things done and build what drives the outcome you seek.

This is not a coordination role, and it is not a strategy-deck role. If your best work has been influencing other teams to build things, this will be a frustrating job. If you have been waiting for a role where you are simply allowed to go and fix it, this is that role.

  • Own delivery: planning with Product, release process, quality and predictability.

  • Own the technical direction of our infrastructure, including deployments, reliability, observability, security and incident readiness.

  • Bring the technical perspective into prioritization, including when to pay down technical debt.

  • Hire and onboard engineers as the team grows.

  • Lead our AI-assisted engineering workflows, including coding agents, reusable agent tooling, evaluations and guardrails.

  • Collaborate with open-source contributors, software vendors and integration partners.

Requirements

What you bring

  • Strong backend and systems architecture skills, ideally with TypeScript and Node.js, and you still write production code regularly.

  • Experience leading an engineering team with people responsibility, as Head of Engineering, Engineering Manager or Tech Lead.

  • Hands-on experience with agent runtimes like LangChain, OpenAI Agent SDK, Mastra or similar.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure, containers, CI/CD, databases, observability and security.

  • Experience designing APIs and integrations, such as OAuth/OIDC, webhooks, synchronization or event-driven systems.

  • Experience hiring engineers and setting up delivery processes in a small, growing team.

  • A pragmatic product mindset: you judge technical decisions by their effect on reliability, delivery speed and customer value.

  • An interest in using and systematically improving AI-assisted software development.

  • Confident communication in German and English.

  • Experience with open-source software, regulated environments or the public sector is helpful but not required.

Our stack

TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, React, TanStack, PostgreSQL, Redis, S3-compatible storage, Docker Compose, Hetzner, GitHub Actions, OpenTelemetry and multiple LLM providers.

No LangChain though – we've built our agent orchestration from the ground up.

title: Head of Hospitals & Home Care
descriptionHtml:
Qui sommes-nous ?

Doctolib est une entreprise B Corp engagée à construire ensemble la santé dont nous rêvons tous. Avec 2 900 collaborateurs en France, en Allemagne, en Italie et aux Pays-Bas, nous accompagnons plus de 420 000 professionnels de santé et 90 millions de patients, transformant l'accès aux soins et la prise en charge à travers l'Europe. Nous accélérons désormais notre ambition : devenir le partenaire clinique de référence en Europe, de confiance pour les patients et les professionnels, grâce à la puissance de technologies avancées et de l'IA.

Notre ambition est de construire le système d'exploitation clinique de demain pour l'Europe - offrant des résultats de santé mesurables pour des millions de personnes.

  • Pour les professionnels de santé : Nous réduisons la charge administrative, augmentons la prise de décision clinique grâce à l'IA et permettons de nouveaux modèles de soins.

  • Pour les patients : Nous passons de soins réactifs en cas de maladie à une gestion proactive de leur santé, en donnant aux personnes les moyens de prendre en charge leur santé avec des compagnons numériques de confiance, recommandés par les médecins.

Vos missions

L'hôpital est clé pour le développement de Doctolib. En une décennie, nous avons construit une présence solide auprès des établissements de santé, publics et privés à but non lucratif, avec une suite complète de solutions couvrant l'ensemble du parcours ambulatoire : visibilité de l'offre de soins, planification, prise de rendez-vous, préparation administrative, assistant de consultation IA, téléconsultation, téléexpertise et bien plus encore.

En tant que Head of Hospitals & Home Care, vous prenez la tête d'une équipe d'une quinzaine de personnes, structurée en acquisition et account management, et appuyée par de nombreuses équipes expertes partenaires, notamment Déploiement, Interopérabilité, Product Marketing et Affaires Publiques. Vous êtes le ou la garant(e) de la performance commerciale, de la satisfaction client et de la vision stratégique du segment hospitalier en France, tout en ouvrant la voie à de nouveaux territoires : le médico-social et les soins à domicile.

Votre responsabilité sera de combiner performance à court terme, développement de la base installée et construction d'une vision stratégique à deux ou trois ans pour le segment.

Vous rejoindrez l'équipe Salaried & Retail France de Doctolib, en reportant à Maric Philibert, notre VP Sales, Salaried & Retail.

Vos responsabilités incluent, mais ne sont pas limitées à :

  • Piloter et atteindre les objectifs de net MRR du segment, sur l'acquisition, l'expansion et la rétention, avec une implication personnelle dans le développement des comptes les plus stratégiques et l'accélération du cross-sell sur les nouvelles solutions, notamment l'Assistant de Consultation et la Téléexpertise.

  • Assurer la satisfaction et l'usage effectif des solutions Doctolib dans les établissements clients, en coordination étroite avec les équipes Déploiement, Interopérabilité et Customer Care.

  • Manager, développer et engager une équipe d'environ 15 personnes, accompagner sa montée en séniorité et renforcer son efficacité grâce à la donnée et aux agents IA.

  • Construire et incarner la vision stratégique à deux ou trois ans du segment, en lien avec la Product Vision de Doctolib et les tendances de marché, en coordination avec les équipes Product Marketing, Affaires Publiques, Communication et Produit.

  • Développer et entretenir les relations institutionnelles clés et piloter les partenariats stratégiques du segment.

  • Explorer et engager Doctolib dans les segments médico-social et soins à domicile, en définissant les besoins, la stratégie et les approches tactiques adaptées.

  • Développer une approche structurée de segmentation, d'account planning et de couverture des comptes stratégiques, afin d'augmenter l'adoption, l'expansion, le cross-sell et la rétention.

  • Coordonner les équipes Tech, Déploiement, Legal, Finance, Product Marketing, Affaires Publiques et Partenariats, tout en gardant les priorités clients et terrain au centre des décisions.

Votre impact

Au cours des 6 premiers mois, vous aurez établi un diagnostic clair et un plan opérationnel pour le segment, renforcé l'équipe et les managers, amélioré la visibilité sur la performance et créé une nouvelle dynamique autour des comptes stratégiques et des opportunités de croissance.

À deux à cinq ans, la réussite se traduira notamment par :

  • Faire progresser le revenu et doubler la croissance en new ARR annuel via l’upsell (licences des solutions historiques), le cross sell (livraison de solutions autour de l’IA et de la coordination des soins) ainsi que l’acquisition de nouveaux clients dans les segments hospitaliers sous-exploités aujourd’hui , le médico-social, les EHPAD et les soins à domicile.

  • Positionner Doctolib comme une solution complète, de confiance et créatrice de valeur pour les établissements de santé, dans une approche plus partenariale et moins transactionnelle, et accompagner les mouvements de fond du secteur : du curatif au préventif, vers plus de coordination entre professionnels de tous types, la responsabilité populationnelle

  • Construire une équipe stable, plus senior et soutenue par les agents IA, donc en capacité de vendre et d’assurer la satisfaction pour plus de solutions et plus d’établissements, moins dépendante des expertises individuelles.

Profil recherché

Nous recherchons un leader senior capable d'agir comme le ou la CEO du segment et d'évoluer avec crédibilité auprès d'interlocuteurs exécutifs internes et externes.

  • Vous justifiez d'une expérience significative auprès d'établissements de santé, acquise comme fournisseur ou prestataire, éditeur e-santé, acteur de la healthtech, dirigeant d'établissement ou de groupe, institutionnel ou consultant en santé avec une forte dimension commerciale. Vous comprenez les acteurs, les personas, les cultures, les rythmes, les circuits de décision et les enjeux politiques et réglementaires du secteur.

  • Vous avez une expérience de la vente B2B complexe et grands comptes, avec des organisations comprenant de nombreuses parties prenantes et des cycles de vente longs. Vous maîtrisez l'acquisition, la vente de solutions complexes, la gestion de comptes stratégiques, l'expansion, l'adoption et la rétention.

  • Vous apportez une vision business 360° couvrant la stratégie, le go-to-market, l'acquisition, l'expansion, les partenariats, le produit, les opérations et l'account management, sans angle mort.

  • Vous avez managé et développé une organisation d'au moins 10 personnes, idéalement composée de profils hétérogènes, avec un historique de transformation, de montée en séniorité et de développement de managers.

  • Vous savez délivrer des résultats à court terme tout en construisant le segment à moyen et long terme, avec rigueur analytique, gravitas C-level et excellente coordination transverse avec Tech, Déploiement, Legal, Finance, Product Marketing, Affaires Publiques et Partenariats.

  • Vous maîtrisez le français et l'anglais, à l'oral comme à l'écrit.

Ce serait un plus si vous aviez aussi :

  • Une expérience des acteurs du médico-social, des EHPAD ou des soins à domicile, ou une forte motivation pour contribuer activement à l'ouverture de ces marchés.

  • Une bonne compréhension des enjeux politiques et réglementaires de la santé numérique, notamment le Ségur du Numérique, l'interopérabilité, les financements publics et les politiques de santé.

  • Une aisance naturelle dans les interactions à dimension institutionnelle ou politique, avec une gravitas adaptée aux interlocuteurs C-level, publics et techniques.

  • Une expérience dans une scale-up, un éditeur e-santé, une direction hospitalière ou de groupe, un acteur institutionnel ou un cabinet de conseil en santé.

Notre offre

  • Une mutuelle avantageuse prise en charge à 100 % par Doctolib pour les employés et leurs enfants

  • 25 jours de congés payés et jusqu'à 14 jours de RTT par an 

  • Un programme de santé mentale et de coaching personnalisé gratuit avec notre partenaire Moka.care

  • Une politique de travail flexible avec 10 jours par an de télétravail possible depuis les pays de l'Union européenne et le Royaume-Uni 

  • Des tickets restaurant d'une valeur de 8,5 € par jour, dont 4,5 € pris en charge par Doctolib

  • Un programme d'intégration complet de 3 mois incluant la Doctolib Academy et diverses formations (langues, soft skills, compétences techniques)

  • Une subvention du comité d'entreprise pour le remboursement partiel d'adhésions à des activités sportives ou de loisirs

  • Un remboursement à 50% de l'abonnement aux transports en commun

  • Un mois de congé supplémentaire au congé parental légal grâce au programme "Parent Care"

  • Aide au déménagement en cas de mobilité internationale

  • Pour les salariés en situation de handicap ou proches aidants, un package comprenant une adaptation du télétravail, des jours d'absence autorisée payés pour les rendez-vous médicaux et un soutien psychologique renforcé

Processus de recrutement

  • Entretien avec un recruteur (45 min)

  • Entretien avec le VP Sales, Salaried & Retail (1h)

  • Cas pratique (1h30)

  • Entretien avec un pair (optionnel) (45 min)

  • Entretien final avec notre Managing Director France

Détails du poste

Chez Doctolib, nous sommes convaincus que nous devons améliorer la santé pour tout le monde. Cela se reflète dans notre processus de recrutement. Nous évaluons les candidatures uniquement sur la base des qualifications et de la motivation, sans aucune forme de discrimination.

Rejoignez-nous pour construire la santé dont nous rêvons tous !

title: Head of Operations
descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.

The Role

The Head of Operations reports to Sauraj (Co-CEO, GTM and Operations) and take ownership of operational excellence company-wide. As Finance, Legal, People, IT and InfoSec, and Compliance grow into their own functions, this person partners with each lead on the operational side of their work and holds the whole together as one system. They lead the operations team and grow it into one fit for a company many times our current size.

  • Builds the operating engine for growth and scale. Owns how the company runs operationally and designs the processes that hold up as headcount, revenue, and complexity grow fast. Everything breaks at each new stage of growth; this person sees it coming and rebuilds ahead of the curve so operations never becomes the ceiling on how fast we can move.

  • Drives operational excellence across every function. Accountable for the operational side of finance, people, legal, and the wider back office, with IT, InfoSec, and compliance covered through the relevant leads. You will set the standard and makes sure nothing important falls between functions.

  • Brings order to ambiguity. Takes the most complex, cross-functional problems and drives them to resolution bringing all the right stakeholder to the table, motivating and inspiring them to come together and deliver the project for everyone’s benefit.

  • Is a decision partner. Frames trade-offs, surfaces risk early, and turns decisions into action, so the leadership team works from reliable data and sound judgment.

  • Builds and inspires the operations team. Hires, develops, and leads an operations team people want to be part of, and sets a standard of execution that raises the bar for everyone who works with them.

Who we're looking for

Essential:

  • High-growth experience above all. Has operated inside a company through rapid scaling, seen what breaks at each stage, and built the processes and structures that scaled through it. This is the most important thing we are looking for.

  • Global operating experience. Has run operations across multiple countries and regions, comfortable holding a company together across time zones and jurisdictions, not just in a single market.

  • Broad operations ownership. Has driven operational excellence across two or more of finance, people, legal, and business operations as a senior generalist, partnering with specialist leads rather than owning their decisions.

  • A leader operators want to follow. Builds and develops strong teams and is the kind of person other excellent operators want to come and work with.

A big plus:

  • Experience in the data, developer tools, or AI market, and comfort working credibly with a technical, research-led team

  • Has built an operations function that grew with a company from startup into real scale

What makes someone thrive here:

  • Energized by building the systems that unlock the next stage of growth, not by maintaining the status quo

  • Radical ownership: runs at the most difficult problems and resolves them rather than passing them up

  • Practical and pragmatic: builds processes that scale without bloat, using as much structure as the moment needs

  • Calm and decisive under ambiguity and competing priorities, and sets that standard for the team

Location

Ideally this person will be located at one of our hubs in New York or Berlin. In exceptional circumstances, we will be able to consider remote/hybrid applications.

Life at Prior Labs

You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right.

Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. But great people come from everywhere, and in exceptional cases we're open to remote, which usually means frequent travel to one of our offices. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together.

Our Commitments

The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. We welcome applications from all identities and walks of life - especially if you've ever felt discouraged by "not checking every box" - and provide equal opportunities regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, disability, or any other trait that makes you who you are.

We care about how your data is handled - see our Recruiting Data Privacy page

title: Head of Region
descriptionHtml:
Help make the world more hospitable

The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.

You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.

If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.

About the role

Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:

What if you could own an entire region, from the first customer conversation to long-term growth?

At Mews, we’re creating a new leadership role for each of our EMEA regions, and we’re hiring the Head of Region for:
Benelux, Italy, Spain, Nordic, UK&IRE, France and DACH.

You’ll bring commercial growth, onboarding and customer success together under one regional strategy, accountable for performance, customer outcomes and the regional P&L within the plan you agree with our VP of EMEA.

This isn’t just about hitting a sales target. It’s about building a regional business where every part of the customer experience works together, from winning a hotel to helping it succeed on Mews.

You’ll report to our VP of EMEA, lead teams across commercial, onboarding and customer success, and have a real say in how we grow, operate and deliver value in the region. 

It’s a rare chance to combine commercial leadership, operational ownership and genuine influence over how we scale.

What you’ll do

Drive growth across the region

Own the regional go-to-market plan, new ARR and revenue from customers going live. You’ll run Business Development, SMB and Mid-Market Sales, Onboarding and Customer Success to win new customers, grow existing relationships and open up opportunities across the region.

Own the entire customer experience

Bring sales, onboarding and customer success together around one goal: making customers successful. From signature and go-live to adoption, renewal and expansion, you’ll make sure hotels experience one connected Mews journey, with a named owner at every hand-off. You’ll build executive relationships with the region’s largest hotels and groups, own recovery plans when a customer is at risk, and work with Product, Marketing and the central support and delivery teams to turn what you hear from customers into better outcomes.

Run the region like a business

Take ownership of the regional P&L within the plan agreed with the VP of EMEA, balancing revenue growth, headcount, capacity and controllable costs. You’ll work closely with Finance and RevOps to make sound commercial decisions and deliver steady performance.

Build and empower exceptional teams

Lead through team leads and senior specialists across commercial, onboarding and customer success. Some of those teams are shared with other regions, so you’ll set up how they work together with the other regional leaders. You’ll create alignment, develop the next layer of leaders and build a culture where teams collaborate, take ownership and deliver results.

Help shape an AI-native business

We’re serious about using AI to change how we work. You’ll lead by example, building AI systems, tools and standards that help your team spot opportunities, make better decisions and spend more time on what matters. You’ll coach others, raise AI fluency across the region and decide where a person has to make the call.

What you would bring

We’re looking for a commercially minded leader who enjoys building businesses, developing people and connecting growth to customer success.

  • A track record of commercial success. 8+ years in B2B SaaS or hospitality commercial roles, including at least 3 years leading teams, consistently taking teams to and beyond target. You’ve owned a commercial number and built the go-to-market plan behind it.
  • End-to-end customer leadership. You’ve led onboarding, customer success, implementation or delivery teams, accountable for time to go-live, adoption, retention and net revenue retention, and you’ve led a team spanning more than one discipline.
  • Business acumen. You’ve owned a P&L or budget, including controllable costs, headcount and margin trade-offs, ideally across commercial and customer delivery teams, and you collaborate on the plan and numbers with Finance and RevOps.
  • An ability to bring people together. You’ve developed talent, built a bench and guided teams through growth or change. You’re fluent in English and the primary language of the region, and comfortable building relationships with customers, colleagues and senior stakeholders.
  • An AI-first mindset backed by action. AI Fluency Level 4, or equivalent hands-on experience: you’ve built AI tools, systems or standards that changed how a team operates, and you can show us what you built, who uses it and what changed.

Even better if you have

  • Experience in hospitality or hotel technology, with an understanding of the challenges hotel operators face.
  • Experience working in a matrix organisation, collaborating with shared teams and influencing stakeholders across regions.

How we think about AI

This role requires AI Fluency Level 4. That means going beyond using AI tools yourself. You’ve built systems, standards or ways of working that others rely on, you coach others on the craft, and you decide what the region acts on when AI flags patterns across it, keeping human oversight in place where it matters.

For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates on Confluence.

Why this role matters

We believe the best customer experience comes from shared ownership of the whole journey. As Head of Region, you’ll make that real shaping not just how we grow, but how we deliver for our customers.

Please note: This role is open to both internal and external candidates. Internal applications are already being considered, and both processes will run in parallel. All candidates will be assessed fairly against the requirements of the role.

Pay Transparency at Mews

What’s in it for you?

Our success is powered by our incredible people, supported by benefits that help them thrive.

Global benefits

No matter where you’re based, you’ll enjoy:

  • Unlimited paid holiday (yes, really)
  • Participation in our company share program
  • Paid parental leave (6 months fully paid for primary caregivers, 2 months for secondary, available after one year of service)

  • Monthly "EDGE" time to Explore, Develop, Grow, and Elevate yourself
  • A work from anywhere policy with flexibility to work abroad for a few weeks each year

  • Flexible, hybrid working options

Local benefits

You'll receive additional benefits that vary by location, from healthcare and retirement plans to team events, socials and other perks. Ask us about it during your interview process.

Life at Mews

We’re an equal opportunities employer. We value teams that reflect the diversity of the customers and communities we serve. Different perspectives make better ideas, stronger products and a more welcoming company.

We also believe transparency is important when deciding if you're the right fit. Mews is an ambitious, high-pressure environment of continuous learning and high standards. Success here requires resilience, adaptability and a willingness to solve difficult problems.

A few things that define how we work:

  • High autonomy means high responsibility. People are expected to take ownership and drive outcomes. There isn’t a detailed playbook for everything, and that’s part of what makes the work challenging – and rewarding.
  • Change is constant. We’re growing quickly and adapting as we scale. Teams, processes and priorities continue to evolve, and only people who stay curious and agile will thrive.
  • We’re remote-first, not relationship-free. Flexibility is core to how we work, but strong relationships still matter. Our teams are global, so we need expert collaborators and communicators to help us move forward together.
  • AI is an integral part of our processes. It’s not here to steal people’s jobs, but to amplify efficiency and productivity. We’re motivated to proactively use the technology to seek out better ways of working and share our findings with the rest of the company.

If there's anything we can do to support you during the application process, let us know.

We don't discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, nationality, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other protected characteristic.

One final thing: don't hold back. If you don't meet 100% of the criteria in this job description but you're certain you could make a big impact, apply. Everyone should have equal access to opportunities, and we're committed to providing an inclusive experience.

If Mews sounds like the kind of environment where you'd thrive, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Image Processing Intern: AI-Assisted Tools for CalVal
descriptionHtml:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft Orbital is looking for an intern to join the End-to-End Validation & Performance (EVP) team and contribute to image-processing and calibration/validation (CAL/VAL) activities for Earth-observation missions. In this internship, you’ll explore how AIT captures and routine onboard imagery can support optical performance testing and radiometric calibration, and turn that work into an evaluated engineering prototype.

Location: Toulouse office, city center (Jeanne d’Arc metro station)
Duration: 6-month, end-of-studies internship — target start date: early 2027.


About this role:
  • Review DSNU, radiometric calibration, and relevant EVP processing and CAL/VAL practices.
  • Work with EVP engineers to identify suitable routine images, metadata, and reference calibration data; document data limitations and provenance.
  • Prepare a reproducible dataset and establish reference baselines, including a holdout evaluation strategy that avoids tuning and testing on the same acquisitions.
  • Implement a baseline estimator: a data-fit term combined with a regularizing prior.
  • Investigate additional AI/ML methods only where suitable training or validation data are available; compare them against the baseline rather than assuming they are superior.
  • Evaluate correction quality, residual fixed-pattern structure, stability across images, runtime, and failure cases.
  • Package the workflow as a prototype script or notebook with plots, quality checks, and an auditable record of inputs, parameters, and outputs.
  • Present findings and recommendations to EVP and CAL/VAL stakeholders; document what evidence would be needed before operational use.
    • The intern will gain experience in:
    • Radiometric calibration and CAL/VAL for space-based optical imaging.
    • Push-broom image characteristics and PRNU/DSNU correction.
    • Applied optimization and, where appropriate, machine learning for image processing.
    • Experimental design, reference-data limitations, and quantitative performance assessment.
    • Building reproducible engineering tools and communicating technical evidence to mission teams.

Must Haves:
  • Student in engineering, applied physics, remote sensing, image processing, data science, or a related field.
  • Fundamentals of signal or image processing and a strong interest in Earth observation.
  • Basic programming skills in Python and comfort working with scientific data.
  • Analytical mindset, rigor, and ability to document assumptions and limitations.
  • Interest in calibration, validation, sensor behavior, or image quality assessment.

Nice to Haves:
  • Exposure to satellite imagery or remote-sensing data.
  • Experience with optimization, statistical estimation, or machine-learning evaluation.
  • Familiarity with image-analysis libraries and scientific Python tools.
  • Understanding of radiometric calibration or data-quality assessment.

What Can We Offer?
You will join a stimulating environment, surrounded by passionate engineers, conducive to learning, innovation, and personal and professional development — and help build the future of space infrastructure. With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, USA | Golden, USA | and Toulouse, France.

Some of our awesome internship benefits:
  • Gratification: €1,300 gross/month.
  • Lunch vouchers (tickets restaurant), because let's be honest, we love food! (we even have a Slack channel about it: #loft-gourmand)
  • Sustainable mobility package (forfait mobilité durable).
  • A genuinely international environment comprising 20+ different nationalities.
  • A genuine mentoring program to support you on a daily basis throughout the internship.
*Research shows that while men apply to jobs where they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other underrepresented people tend to only apply when they meet 100% of the qualifications. At Loft, we value respectful debate and people who aren’t afraid to challenge assumptions. We strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don’t check all the boxes.
Who We Are
Loft: Space Made Simple.
Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit.
We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. With more than 30 missions flown, Loft’s flight heritage and proven technologies enable customers to focus on their mission objectives.
With a growing fleet on track to reach 30 satellites by 2027, we are scaling up quickly across our offices in San Francisco, CA | Golden, CO | and Toulouse, France to meet accelerating demand for space infrastructure.
As an international company your resume will be reviewed by people across our offices so please attach a copy in English.

title: Industrial Data & Solutions Engineer (gn) @ Stealth AI Venture, Berlin
descriptionHtml:
This is an Atlantic portfolio company.

What we're building

Factories run on machines that generate huge amounts of data, and almost none of it gets used. We're changing that. We build AI software that helps production engineers and operators turn machine data into answers: why a line is slowing down, what's causing scrap, and what to fix next. We're early and in stealth. Our two founders both held C-level roles at leading German robotics ventures. They have spent years bringing advanced technology onto real shop floors, and now they're hiring the founding core team.

Your role & responsibility

You're the person who makes our product work in the real world. You go into a plant, figure out what's actually broken, connect the data, and stay until operators use the product every day without being asked. You'll work with everyone from the machine operator to the plant manager, and with IT and OT. You own each customer from the first conversation through rollout and expansion. Berlin or home-based in Germany, with regular time in Berlin with the team. You'll spend about 20% of your time at customer sites.

What you'll do

  • Own deployments end to end: use-case definition, data onboarding, validation, rollout, training, and adoption

  • Turn messy production problems into clear data, analytics, and solution requirements

  • Onboard and validate machine, process, quality, and maintenance data from industrial systems

  • Spot data problems that only make sense if you understand the machine behind them

  • Build and validate KPIs, features, anomaly signals, calibration methods, and analytical workflows in Python and SQL, using statistics and time-series analysis

  • Run the project with the customer and our commercial lead: plans, workshops, validation sessions, and success criteria

  • Find the next machine, line, data source, or use case, and expand with it

  • Bring what you learn in the field back to the product, so each deployment makes the platform better

  • Help write the playbook for how we deliver, as the customer engineering team grows

You might be a fit if you

  • Have worked hands-on with industrial machines and production processes, in manufacturing, automation, maintenance, quality, industrial engineering, or industrial data

  • Know your way around PLCs, SCADA, MES, historians, production databases, quality systems, or OPC UA

  • Use Python and SQL to answer questions, not just to write code

  • Have worked with time-series data, KPIs, anomaly detection, or root-cause analysis

  • Communicate as well on the shop floor as in the plant manager's office

  • Like solving hard problems in automation and process engineering

  • Take ownership, work independently, and are comfortable when things are ambiguous

  • Are happy to travel to customer sites and have a driver's license

  • Speak fluent German and English

Key Account Manager DACH (all genders)

Als Key Account Manager DACH (all genders) bei tonies bist du die strategische Schnittstelle zwischen unseren Produkten und den führenden Handelsunternehmen der DACH-Region. Mit Verhandlungsgeschick, strategischem Weitblick und einer großen Portion Begeisterung steuerst du unsere wichtigsten Accounts, hebst Umsatzpotenziale und trägst maßgeblich dazu bei, unsere Marktposition langfristig auszubauen.

  • Eine enge Abstimmung und effektive Zusammenarbeit mit allen relevanten internen Schnittstellen sind für dich selbstverständlich

  • Du bist ca. 20% deiner Zeit on the road, d.h. besuchst regelmäßig die Kundenzentralen und nimmst aktiv an branchenspezifischen Messen teil

Das bringst Du mit

  • Du bringst eine kaufmännische Ausbildung oder ein abgeschlossenes Studium mit und hast mindestens drei Jahre Erfahrung als nationaler Key Account Manager*in mit direktem Kundenkontakt.

  • Jahresgespräche und unterjährige Preisverhandlungen hast du aktiv mitgestaltet und entwickelst deine Verhandlungsstärke kontinuierlich weiter.

  • Du kennst den deutschen Einzelhandel und die Spielwarenbranche gut. Erfahrung in der Betreuung von Drogeriemärkten ist ein echter Pluspunkt.

  • Du knüpfst mit Leichtigkeit Kontakte, überzeugst durch herausragende soziale Kompetenz und gehst mit Leidenschaft in Verhandlungen.

  • Als Teamplayer arbeitest du konstruktiv mit deinen Kolleg:innen zusammen, hörst ihren Ideen zu und erreichst mit uns gemeinsam ehrgeizige Ziele.

  • Analytisches Denken liegt dir im Blut: Du gehst sicher mit Daten um und triffst damit fundierte Entscheidungen. Du arbeitest dich schnell in neue Tools und Systeme ein (z. B. Google-Produkte, Tableau, Slack) und vermittelst auch technische Zusammenhänge verständlich.

  • Du kommunizierst verhandlungssicher auf Deutsch und Englisch und besitzt einen Führerschein der Klasse B. Dafür stellen wir dir ein Fahrzeug für dienstliche und private Fahrten zur Verfügung.

Warum tonies?

  • Globale Teamarbeit: Wir arbeiten gemeinsam über Abteilungs- und Ländergrenzen hinweg an unserer Vision, die Toniebox in alle Kinderzimmer der Welt zu bringen.

  • Come as you are: Das gilt nicht nur für den Dresscode, sondern auch für alles andere. Denn nur wo du dich wirklich wohlfühlst, kannst du auch dein Bestes geben.

  • Mobilität: Wähle das Angebot, das am besten zu dir passt – ein Deutschlandticket Job für uneingeschränkte Mobilität, eine monatliche Zuzahlung von fünfzig Euro für einen Büro-Parkplatz, ein Leasing-Fahrrad oder als Remote Work Zuschuss.

  • Absicherung: Profitiere von Zuschüssen zu vermögenswirksamen Leistungen, einer betrieblichen Altersvorsorge und einer Berufsunfähigkeitsversicherung.

  • Erholung & Auszeit: Genieße 30 Tage bezahlten Jahresurlaub sowie drei zusätzliche freie Tage wie Rosenmontag, Heiligabend und Silvester. Nach einem Jahr Betriebszugehörigkeit kannst du zudem bis zu 10 "toniecation days" (unbezahlte Urlaubstage) nutzen.

Zu unseren Grundsätzen gehört es, dass wir uns bei tonies® für Inklusion und Vielfalt einsetzen. Wir feiern die unterschiedlichen Fähigkeiten, Herkünfte, Glaubensvorstellungen und geschlechtlichen Identitäten, die sich unter unserem Dach vereinen. title: Lead Data Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Better Collective

Sports media at scale, running on data

Better Collective is a global sports media group, reaching more than 400 million monthly visits across a portfolio of leading sports media brands.

We build products and experiences that make sports more engaging and accessible for fans around the world. Behind that sits a large and diverse technology and data landscape, spanning markets, brands and business models.

We work in a collaborative environment where people are encouraged to challenge how things are done, take ownership and help shape what comes next.

The domain

Paid media is where the data has to pay off.

We spend real money across dozens of ad networks every day. Which campaigns scale, which creatives get cut, which markets get more budget: those calls come out of the models this team builds.

Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue, CRM data, all stitched into one user-level view of what a click was actually worth. That model exists and it works.

It is also the most demanding domain on our data platform - the most sources, the fastest schema churn, and the shortest patience for a table that landed late.

We are looking for the engineer who owns it.

Where this role sits

A central platform team sets the how. You set the what.

Better Collective runs a hub and spoke data organisation. A central data platform team owns the platform itself - MotherDuck, dbt, Dagster, DLT, the golden paths, the standards, the infrastructure. Paid Media Insights is a domain team, a spoke, that builds on it.

The split is deliberate and we hold to it. The platform team decides how data is produced here. You decide what paid media produces, and you own everything we run.

So you are not starting a new stack, and you are not going to spend your year on plumbing that a central team should be solving once for everyone.

You are, however, expected to be a demanding customer. When a golden path does not fit paid media, we want you to say so and push for it to change, not quietly build around it.

You will report to the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights and work across Paid Media, with the Campaign, Commercial and CRM teams, as well as with the central platform team.

What you will own

Every data job in paid media. All of it.

Freshness, cost, reliability, alerting, and the incident at 07:30 before the spend review. If a paid media model is wrong or late, it is yours, not the platform team's. That accountability is the core of this role, not a footnote to it.

Concretely, you will own:

  • The end-to-end user-level model. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue, and CRM, joined into one view the business trusts enough to move budget on.

  • Ingestion of paid media sources, built on the platform's framework. Which sources, which schemas, and what happens the next time a network changes its API without telling anyone.

  • The domain's models, from staging through to the marts analysts and business teams actually query, plus the semantic meaning that sits on top of them. Nobody at the centre can define what a qualified signup means in paid media. You can.

  • Reverse ETL back into the ad platforms, so online and offline conversion data lands where it changes bidding.

  • The handover. Part of your first year is taking over the paid media jobs the central team still runs on our behalf, and moving that ownership to where the context actually lives.

What you will lead

A group of engineers, and the standard they build to

You will guide and mentor a group of data engineers in Paid Media Insights, as their technical lead. That means setting the standard for how this domain builds, reviewing their work, unblocking them, and deliberately growing them: giving away the interesting problems rather than keeping them.

You will also shape the domain's roadmap together with the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights, the analysts and the business teams, and you will represent paid media in platform conversations, including how we support machine learning and data science on top of this data.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role, not a step away from building. You will be in the code.


What we are looking for

More than a stack match, we are looking for a particular way of working.

You take ownership, and it shows up in the boring parts. Plenty of engineers want to design the model. You also want the pager. You would rather own a domain end to end, unglamorous parts included, than build one piece and hand off the consequences. When things get tricky, you follow through.

You break complex systems into simple parts. Paid media data is genuinely messy: attribution windows, late conversions, identity across platforms, and dozens of source APIs that all disagree. You can hold that complexity and still hand the business something they can reason about.

You raise the people around you. You are the person colleagues come to for technical advice, and you enjoy that part of the job. You give feedback that lands, you review generously, and you would rather the whole team understand the pipeline than be the only one who does.

You work well with a platform team. You have strong opinions about standards and you are still happy to work inside someone else's. You know the difference between a constraint worth fighting and a preference worth dropping, and you would rather help fix a shared path than fork it.

You are already past prompting. AI is part of how you engineer, not something you occasionally ask questions. You have experimented with agents, tooling or AI-enabled workflows, and you have a view on what a data domain has to look like for them to be useful on top of it: documented, standardised, semantically clear. Paid media is likely where we find out first.

You are close to the business. You will sit with marketers and analysts who are spending budget on what you build. You want that proximity, and you can talk about data with people who do not think in tables.

You are technically deep where it counts. Production pipelines in SQL and Python, modelling and orchestration tooling such as dbt and Dagster, cloud data warehousing, and a real feel for performance, cost and reliability at scale. Experience with paid media or attribution data, or with machine learning pipelines, is a bonus rather than a requirement.

Not sure you meet every single requirement? That is okay. Your unique experience might be exactly what we are looking for.

Our stack

What you will build on

MotherDuck / DuckDB · dbt · Dagster · DLT · Python · SQL · AWS · reverse ETL and semantic layer tooling

We do not expect you to have worked with all of these. If you have built production pipelines on Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift and you are curious about where we are going, that transfers.

What we offer

An international company in growth, and a flat structure

Join a strong team where you can create value and make a real business impact, in a dynamic and creative environment with a flat organisational structure. Freedom with responsibility, ample room to grow, and the chance to take on a broad set of responsibilities.

Flexible working hours supporting a healthy work-life balance, private health insurance, and office perks including lunch, snacks, gym access and social events, alongside skilled, passionate and fun colleagues.

Your path to Better Collective

How to apply

We process applications on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible. For questions about the position, reach out to Michael Hill, Senior Head of Paid Media Insights, at ----- We look forward to hearing from you.
